enemies.name: 17th Collossus
enemies.description:
What happened to the previous sixteen Colossi? They're an urban legend, officially considered fiction despite persistent rumors. Why the heck did we start at number seventeen for this one, then? I'm seriously asking.
We know one thing for sure - the Colossus is a beautiful and peaceful beast, beloved by all. Can you imagine ever hurting something so precious, so innocent, so dedicated to the art of minding its own adorable business? You'd have to be a world class coglione to even consider it.
Almost as bad as letting a horse fall to its presumed death without bothering to see if it's okay.
17th Collossus is an enemy that appears in Mazerella.

enemies.name: Abraxas
enemies.description:
Is it a god, is it a demon, or is it just a chicken that got really, really big? Science has suggested the latter, but contractual obligation to make this book as spicy as possible suggests some fowl combination of the first two things, thus satisfying the further obligation to refer to at least one creature from the Coop as "fowl.". Who doesn't love a bit of birdplay?
Abraxas is an enemy that appears in The Coop. It first appears as a boss in that stage before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Abraxas Dynamis
enemies.description:
Chicken Wizardry is one of the oldest forms of magic a sage can perform. Some say it's just regular magic with a tenuously shoehorned bird theme, but take not lightly the dark powers of peckromancy. Not only can it make chickens run around after losing their heads, it gave rise to the most dreaded monster of all - a palette swap with buffed stats!
Abraxas Dynamis is an enemy that appears in The Coop. It first appears as a boss in that stage before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Abraxas Phronesis
enemies.description:
The finest of the feathered fiends, moving gracefully even while stamping on their victium' skulls with such brutality we coined the term "head porridge." Many heads have been porridged, and at least one was mueslied, in the merciless march of the Abraxas Crown.. Despite their advanced intelligence, they can still be fooled by a leaf-covered hole and a sign reading "free bird seed."
Abraxas Phronesis is an enemy that appears in The Coop. It first appears as a boss in that stage before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: AccumulaTori
enemies.description:
A fully morphed Torino, artificially evolved by lactomantic magicks. While they no longer yield dairy produce, any milk they consume is processed iun the digestive system and comes out as a delicious spreadable.
The creation process may give a layperson pause, but let's be honest, it ranks fairly low on the list of disgusting things a cheese connoisseur is willing to try.
AccumulaTori is an enemy that appears in Mazerella.

enemies.name: Archdemon
enemies.description:
Big. Red. Horny. It really doesn’t get much more demonic than that. Arch Demons strive to exemplify all that it means to be a demon, and they’re diabolically good at it. They swear a lot, too.
Archdemon is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Boss Rash. In Cappella Magna, it appears as both a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Archdemon takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant's health is also base on the player's level.

enemies.name: Archon Ascia
enemies.description:
The least fancy of all Archons, but perhaps the most effective. Marching methodically into battle with a big axe and shield might be boring, but it gets the job done.
Archon Ascia is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Cappella Magna, and Boss Rash. It has a normal variation, which only appears as a normal enemy in Dairy Plant, and a boss variant, which only appears as a boss.
Archon Ascia takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant's health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Archon Disco
enemies.description:
A deluxe model Archon featuring the exact same stats at twice the price. Sold as a luxury defense option, its sheer size and impressive strength do much to hide the fact it’s mostly made of recycled infantry helmets and old buckets.
Archon Disco is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, Boss Rash, and Mazerella. In Gallo Tower and Mazerella, it appears both as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Archon Disco takes increased knockback. Its boss variant instead takes reduced knockback, its health is based on the player's level and it is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Archon Fiamma
enemies.description:
An automated soldier with a tendency to overheat and catch fire. Rather than fix the problem, Gallo Tower claimed it was a feature instead of a bug, and sold these flame-wreathed safety violations to a cabal of demons who gave them great user reviews.
Archon Fiamma is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Archon Lancia
enemies.description:
An Archon model designed to respond to a wide variety of commands, provided those commands involve stabbing something with a long sharp stick.
Archon Lancia is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Archon Oro
enemies.description:
Gilded automatons drafted into service by the Most Holy Order to keep the peace. They didn’t so much keep the peace as keep breaking all the fancy stained glass with their mindless lumbering. They’re as expensive as they look.
Archon Oro is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Archon Oro takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Archon Rame
enemies.description:
“When in doubt, make the sword bigger.” This design philosophy was key to the creation of the Rame, which also boasts the upper body strength required to lift said sword more than a foot off the ground.
Archon Rame is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna, Boss Rash and Tiny Bridge. In Cappella Magna, it first appears as a normal enemy and later also as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss. When it appears as a boss, it can drop a Treasure Chest.
Archon Rame takes reduced knockback and its boss variant's health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Archon Spada
enemies.description:
The twisted result of science and sorcery, these animated suits of armor were mass produced at Gallo Tower as one of its most profitable creations. The sword’s size is terrifying, but woefully impractical, rendering it too heavy to be swung. That hardly matters when it can still mash you like some sort of genocidal butter churner.
Archon Spada is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and Boss Rash. In Gallo Tower, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Archon Spada takes increased knockback. Its boss variant instead takes reduced knockback, its health is based on the player's level and it is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Astral Chair
enemies.description:
Those aware of the rare corner of the astral realm in which matter and soul blend into fair new configurations have learned to fear the Astral Chair. To share the air of the dread Chair is to invite wear and tear on the body bare. But what do you care?
Astral Chair is an enemy that appears in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Astral Curtain
enemies.description:
There are rumors about these robes being sentient demons, capable of entangling unsuspecting bystanders and forcing them to do their devious bidding. They are said to appear when someone forgets to close the windows in very tall towers.
Astral Curtain is an enemy that appears in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Astral Elemental
enemies.description:
Creatures of the stars, attuned to the syncopated rhythms of the cosmos. Untouchable to those not aligned with the correct astronomical wavelengths. Either that, or they're just a bunch of mad lads who like to boogie down.
Astral Elemental is a group of enemies that appear in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Avatar Infernas
enemies.description:
Avatar Infernas is a special enemy that appears in inverse Inlaid Library. Defeating Avatar Infernas for the first time unlocks him as a playable character.
Unlike most enemies, Avatar does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but spawns under certain conditions in inverted Inlaid Library after obtaining Yellow Sign and Greatest Jubilee.
Avatar Infernas is resistant to knockback, freeze, instant kill effects, such as Pentagram and Rosary, and debuffs.
__TOC__

enemies.name: Avatar of Gaea
enemies.description:
When the very natural order is under threat, a great coalescence of all life’s benevolence manifests in corporeality a being of such grace and beauty as to bring civilizations to their knees in awe. The purest embodiment of that which is virtuous and true, the very heart of the planet given form. It once caved a man’s head in with its hoof for peeing in the lake. Blood and bits of skull everywhere.
Avatar of Gaea is a boss that appears in Lake Foscari. It gains more health based on the amount of enemies killed this run. Defeating it in Lake Foscari unlocks the stage's hyper mode. It takes reduced knockback and it is resistant to freeze and debuffs.
It also makes an appearance in the special starting event of The Coop, assuming the player did not kill any Chickenfantries for an entire minute for the first time. In that stage, they are not an enemy or boss that can be killed.

enemies.name: Awizotl
enemies.description:
One would imagine the prehensile-grabby-hand-tail-thing of an Awizotl would be used to snag prey, but shocking, these wet pets were created by the ancient arcanists of the Lycaeum to be excellent jugglers. Consigned to live underwater when the Lycaeum collapsed to the bed of a lake, they are completely unable to serve their ball-throwing purpose, causing immeasurable feline fury that they unleash at every opportunity.
Awizotl is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Bambaman
enemies.description:
Where are all the snowman when it's not the festive season? Here.
Bambaman is an enemy that appears in Whiteout.

enemies.name: Barm
enemies.description:
Barms are sworn to protect scrolls of great literary significance, though the parchments they guard all feature drawings of dubious educational value. It's best not to describe the pictures, so let's just say major credit card companies are pushing to have them censored.
Barm is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Bat Dragon
enemies.description:
Bat Dragon
Bat Dragon is an enemy that appears in specific stages after obtaining the Green Eyes Vizard relic.
Initially the stages can be identified by observing the stage icons pulsating from normal to pitch black with only glowing eyes of Bat Dragon left visible. Once defeated, the pulsation no longer occurs.
The Bat Dragon's position in the Milky Way Map is indicated by a Question Mark Black black question mark in Mad Forest and Il Molise. Before the fight, the Bat Dragon is indicated through a black silhouette. Once engaged and the fight begins, the stage timer is stopped until the Bat Dragon has been defeated, akin to Big Fuzz and the following Ode to Castlevania stage bosses: Beelzebub, Doppelganger, and Legion.
Defeating one Bat Dragon unlocks the Unearthly Bolt. If the player defeated two unique Bat Dragons, the player will be able to purchase the Enemahs. If the player uses Big Troubler to defeat a Bat Dragon while having the Game Killer (0) in hand, they will unlock the Stake to Your Heart (0) Darkana.

enemies.name: Bat Drakelet
enemies.description:
Bat Drakelet
Bat Drakelet is an enemy that appears near Bat Dragons.

enemies.name: Big Golem
enemies.skills: HP x Level (boss and LV29 variants only)
enemies.description:
Big, Big Golem! Put it together, and what do you get? The Big Big Golem Construction Set! Load it up! Truck along! Dump it out! Big Big Golem!
Big Golem is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant and Boss Rash. It appears both as a normal enemy and a boss.
Big Golem takes reduced knockback. Additionally, its boss and LV29 variants are also based on the player's level and are resistant to freeze, instant kill effects, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Big Mummy
enemies.description:
Despite appearances, these shambling cadavers change their bandages daily. Whatever’s going on underneath all those wrappings remains a mystery, but one presumes it’s thoroughly disgusting.
Big Mummy is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with additional appearances in Inlaid Library and Boss Rash.
In Mad Forest, it appears as both a normal enemy and a boss. In Inlaid Library and Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a boss.
Big Mummy is semi-resistant to knockback. Its boss variant has health that scales with the player's level and is partially resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Bloodbath
enemies.description:
Foul ichor seems to ooze from every pore of this creature’s slick skin, leading many to believe that it bathes in the blood of the freshly slain. Closer study reveals their fur is simply red, however. They’re bats, and nothing more.
Bloodbath is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Boon Marrabbio
enemies.description:
Boon Marrabbio is a special enemy that appears in Mad Forest. Defeating Boon Marrabbio for the first time unlocks him as a playable character.
Unlike most enemies, Boon Marrabbio does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but spawns under certain conditions in Mad Forest after obtaining Yellow Sign.
Boon Marrabbio is resistant to knockback, instant kill effects, such as Pentagram and Rosary, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Bounty Hunter
enemies.description:
"Why do angels keep invading that rusty, dusty old workshop? They're supposed to be invading my church!" After making a cavalcade of such envious complaints, the Cardinal finally opened up their vast coffers and paid these Bounty Hunters to prevent anyone from getting into or out of the Laborratory. They've been prowling the corridors of Santa Ladonna's old haunt for a few years now, each trying to figure out a way to escape without the others noticing.
Bounty Hunter is an enemy that appears in Laborratory.

enemies.name: Buklavaca
enemies.description:
If you put a frog in boiling water, it will jump out. If you put a frog in cold water and slowly heat it up, you're being weird. If you put a frog in the arcanely-tainted waters of the Lycaeum, it'll eventually turn into one of these big aggressive amphibians, yet another reason why it really isn't safe to be down there at all.
Buklavaca is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Card Sharp
enemies.description:
On reflection, the keychain guy might be onto something. If I write a bunch of vague nonsense and arbitrarily redact half the words, we'll be knee deep in fan theories and selling plush dolls by the boatload. I bet the dimwit proles will eat it up.
(Note to self: remove this incriminating note before sending the latest volume for publication)
Card Sharp is an enemy that appears in Westwoods and Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Chickenfantry
enemies.description:
Tired of being expected to surrender a tenth of their eggs to humankind, the chickens launched a violent rebellion. Perhaps the hen tithe was a mistake. Now it is we who shall be sent to the other side as the world becomes a clucking hell.
Chickenfantry is an enemy that appears in The Coop.
At the beginning of The Coop, a singular Chickenfantry would spawn at a time, until the player kills their first Chickenfantry. After that, the stage's timer will be activated and a horde of Chickenfantries will spawn.

enemies.name: Chik
enemies.description:
Initial waves of chicken violence went unreported as nobody wanted to admit they'd just been savaged by a gang of adorable baby birds. One man bled to death rather than admit his arms had been chewed off, insisting he still had both hands even as they digested in the belly of the brood.. They're so cute though!
Chik is an enemy that appears in The Coop.

enemies.name: City Atlantean
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, Il Molise, Moongolow, Green Acres, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash
enemies.description:
Powerful guardian of a race long thought extinct. Its mask represents advanced civilization, mastery of the world, social order, and littering.
City Atlantean is an enemy that appears in all normal, bonus and challenge stages. Unlike most enemies, it does not spawn as part a wave or map event, but spawns upon approaching the Metaglio Left, which is one of the hidden stage items unlocked by obtaining the Yellow Sign.

enemies.name: Cockreliutennant
enemies.description:
Anyone who refused to take the poultry rebellion seriously received a wake up call when these guys appeared. Each cock is a hardened gallus and happy to crow about it, commanding the chickenfantry so humanity's hubris may come home to roost.
Cockreliutennant is an enemy that appears in The Coop. It appears as a normal enemy and a boss in that stage.

enemies.name: Colossal Panther
enemies.description:
Colossal Panther is an enemy that appears in Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss.
Colossal Panther's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback. It is also resistant to freeze, instant kill and debuffs.

enemies.name: Containers
enemies.description:
Containers are enemies that can appear in Il Molise, Moongolow, Lake Foscari tf, and Abyss Foscari tf. In Il Molise, they appear as a boss in most waves, and later as a normal enemy. In Moongolow, they appear in an map event lasting throughout the stage, where a cluster of amphoras spawns every 10 seconds at the edges of the screen. In Lake Foscari and Abyss Foscari, they spawn at specific locations, while the pots can be spawn as a pressure plate event.
Containers cannot move and take no knockback. When killed, Anforas and crates drops a Gold Coin instead of experience and is automatically collected. In Moongolow, if the player moves too far from the amphora, it will teleport back into the player's screen.

enemies.name: Cosmic Egg
enemies.description:
When the great many-faced god of all things encounrered the empty void, the void spoke thus, "Canst thou provide substance? Canst thou provide form?" And the many-faced god answered thus, "As a tonic for thy formless sorrow, I shall create a beginning of things. An embryonic gift, thinly shelled in the atomic matter of a new universe, and containing a concentration of reality." In modern english: "Can I offer you a cosmic egg in this trying time?"
The Cosmic Egg is an enemy that appears in Astral Stair. It is unique in that it intermittently casts a large, circular rainbow-colored pulse identical to that of the Infinite Corridor, which also causes the player character's health to be halved if they are inside of its radius. This makes Cosmic Eggs dangerous enemies to defeat regardless of the player's build.
The Cosmic Egg's health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is resistant to, freeze, debuffs, and instant kill.

enemies.name: Count
enemies.description:
Count was an enemy that appeared in Inlaid Library. It only appeared as a boss and had a chance to drop a Treasure Chest.
Count's health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Cute Molisano
enemies.description:
A Molisano that you could introduce to your parents.
Cute Molisano is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Cute Molisano cannot move and it can only deal damage by being touched by the player. Though, O'Sole Meeo does not take damage if it touches this enemy.
This enemy gains additional health if the Celestial Dusting interacts with it.

enemies.name: Daimon
enemies.description:
There's this guy selling keychains of these things who keeps asking me to make them "a thing." I refuse to burn my integrity by contriving merchandisable horror "lore" for these weird goblins. They're just stinky little guys, and there's nothing deeper to them.
Daimon is an enemy that appears in Westwoods. It first appears as a boss for a few waves, then appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Dandybrine
enemies.description:
Female and fem-presenting dragons who assist the Barms in their safekeeping of tasteful adult media. They're completely loyal to the sauce material.
Dandybrine is an enemy that appears in Westwoods. It first appears as a boss for a few waves, then appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Dead Molisano
enemies.description:
A Molisano that doesn’t really do much at all because it’s really, really dead.
Dead Molisano is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It first appears a boss and later also as a normal enemy. When it appears as a boss, it drops a Treasure Chest.
Dead Molisano cannot move and it can only deal damage by being touched by the player. Though, O'Sole Meeo does not take damage if it touches this enemy.
This enemy gains additional health if the Celestial Dusting interacts with it.

enemies.name: Deep Angellette
enemies.description:
As above, so below. These strange seraphs rise from the depths of the lake bed, rumored to be angels that fled the chaos in Capella Magna, only to find that not everything is better down where its wetter. Whatever their divine providence, their celestial song vibrates through water with perfect quality, harmonising with the rumbles of Deep Angellette to form a choir that tugs and twists the soul.
Deep Angellette is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Deep Sluge
enemies.description:
Considered a delicacy by absolutely nobody, these cutey-crawlies combine all the slimy wetness of a regular surface slug with the magical dampness of the lakebed. I don't think they have any idea of the arcane significance of the Lycaeum, or that Moongolow is just around the corner - in fact, I'm not even sure they have brains.
Deep Sluge is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Deep Sphynx
enemies.description:
Eldest and soggiest of all the Lycaeum's guardians, they pose riddles to all who dare trespass in those hallowed, sunken halls. Since nobody has figured out how to talk underwater, the only answer a Deep Sphynx has ever gotten to a riddle is "glub glub", which has made them so mad they've just started attacking people.
Deep Sphynx is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Demon Beast
enemies.description:
Moved into Cappella Magna after the Order’s decisive fall. Spreading depravity and debasement wherever they roam, the Demon Beasts satisfy every wicked desire that crosses their lewd minds. Seriously, these guys are into some nasty, nasty stuff.
Demon Beast is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Demon Beast takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Demon Priest
enemies.description:
When the Most Holy Order began ordaining literal demons, some suggested that perhaps the integrity of the system had been compromised. What foolishness. The system had no integrity to begin with.
Demon Priest is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Demon Priest takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Diamond
enemies.description:
Diamonds are event enemies that appear in Bat Country. They appear periodically throughout the stage in Monster Dance, Diamond Road, Diamond Square and Diamond Maze events, sometimes bouncing up from the bottom of the screen and other times appearing in various formations around the player.
Diamonds take no knockback and usually do not move, unless they are bouncing upwards from the bottom of the screen. Upon spawning, Diamonds are blue. Each time they get hit, they change color, turning green, then yellow, then pink. After getting hit four times, they die. When they are killed, they drop coins and pickups, similarly to a light source.

enemies.name: Dragon Shrimp
enemies.description:
When a shrimp yearns to be a dragon above all things, the Horned Shrimp may take pity on it and bestow a form most mighty. Or rather, a form almost mighty. It turns out that being the patron god of all shrimp doesn’t let you make anything much more intimidating than this, but the shrimp are happy!
Dragon Shrimp is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, Boss Rash and The Bone Zone. It first appears as an map event enemy and later also as a normal enemy and a boss. The "flag" variants appear in the Dragon Stream, Dragon Swarm, and Skeleton Stream events, whereas the regular variants spawn periodically during waves. The boss variant appears both as a normal and boss enemy.
Killing 3,000 Dragon Shrimps is the requirement for unlocking O'Sole Meeo. This count does not include the unlisted Dragon Shrimp variants.
Dragon Shrimp's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback. The flag variant's movement is fixed on horizontal axis.

enemies.name: Dust Elemental
enemies.stages: Inlaid Library, Boss Rash, Laborratory, Eudaimonia Machine
enemies.description:
If knowledge is not known, it ceases to be knowledge. The Inlaid Library’s virulent swell of forbidden lore yearns to inscribe itself into an open mind. Left for decades with only dust for company, that lore made a home for itself. Fortunate are we that the Dust Elementals have no tongue to speak it.
Dust Elemental is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, Laborratory, Boss Rash, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Inlaid Library and Boss Rash, it appears both as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Laborratory, it appears as a normal enemy and as parts of map events. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.
Its boss variant's health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: ECMASlime
enemies.description:
These blobs are actually super friendly and just want to deliver you a pleasant Experience. Unfortunately, they aren't aware that their bodies are composed of a slightly acidic slime.
ECMASlime is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Egge
enemies.description:
These crack troops are often used as ordnance, their shellfire creating a yolk of suppression. Always in the vanguard, they arrive before the chickens do. Even if we're overthrown by killer birds, it's nice to have settled that debate.
Egge is an enemy that appears in The Coop.

enemies.name: Eh'Lleve-Teh Darkasso
enemies.description:
After witnessing mortal heroes "dual-wielding" two weapons at once, devilish fleshcrafters decided to one-up their corporeal enemies, creating these demonic golems capable of quad-wielding four forsaken hellblades at once. Due to an unreasonable infernal deadline the fleshcrafters didn't actually have time to make them any weapons, leaving the Eh'Lleve-Teh Darkasso unarmed with a minor case of impostor syndrome.
Eh'Lleve-Teh Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Elite Devil
enemies.description:
Elite Devil is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. It only appears as a boss.
Elite Devil's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Enypnastys
enemies.description:
When this magical sub-species of jellyfish blushes, their translucent membrane turns completely sea-through. Unfortunately, they find having their innards on display in this way incredibly embarrassing, causing them to blush even more in a vicious (and potentially viscous) cycle of awkwardness.
Enypnastys is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Fake Fallen Cherub
enemies.description:
Fake Fallen Cherub is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Holy Forbidden. In Cappella Magna, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Holy Forbidden, it appears both as a normal enemy and as a special enemy spawned by The Maddener.
Fake Fallen Cherub originally looks like a bat but takes an angelic form in Maddener's presence.

enemies.name: Fake Fallen Cherubbello
enemies.description:
Fake Fallen Cherubbello is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Holy Forbidden. In Cappella Magna, it first appears as a boss and later also as a normal enemy. In Holy Forbidden, it appears as a special enemy spawned by The Maddener.
Fake Fallen Cherubbello originally looks like a bat, but changes appearance in Maddener's presence. The normal variant takes reduced knockback. The boss variant's health is based on the player's level. The variant in Holy Forbidden has a self-destruct attack, which triggers immediately after spawning. After 2 seconds it explodes dealing 50 damage.

enemies.name: Fallen Cherub
enemies.description:
Former personifications of innocence, their harmonious chorus once sang the glory of the Heavens. Now they sing of despair and destruction, of infidelity and indecency, of torment, torture, and mixing trash with recycling.
Fallen Cherub is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Fallen Cherub takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Fallen Cherubbello
enemies.description:
Porcelain faced miscreants that chant incessantly and ring their bells when others are trying to sleep. Even before their turn to evil, they were famed for being annoying and just a little bit creepy.
Fallen Cherubbello is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Fallen Cherubbello takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Fallen Throne
enemies.description:
Angelic abominations whose beauty belies a malevolent intent. Soaked in vice, their every whim is a sick contradiction of the virtues they once extolled.
Fallen Throne is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Fallen Throne takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Flower Wall
enemies.description:
Said to have first sprouted during a total eclipse of the sun, these blighted blooms appear when they are least needed, which is to say they appear all the time.
Flower Wall is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with additional appearances in Mt.Moonspell lm and Lake Foscari tf.
In Mad Forest, it first appears during the Flower Wall map event and later reappears as a normal enemy in later waves. In Mt.Moonspell and Lake Foscari, it appears during Circle map events and as a special enemy that spawns at specific, fixed locations on the map.
Flower Wall's health scales with the player's level, except for the Foscari variant. Movement speed varies by type: the base variant moves very slowly, the Foscari variant is as fast as most enemies, and both Moonspell variants are immobile. Knockback resistance also differs: the base and Foscari variants take reduced knockback, Moonspell 1 is semi-resistant, and Moonspell 2 is fully resistant.

enemies.name: Foo'Ori Darkasso
enemies.description:
Technically shapeshifters, these unpredictable terror-dogs have all chosen to maintain the form of a horrible hell-hound, finding perfect for mauling their enemies and enjoying demonic belly rubs. Though typically deployed as sentinels guarding the gates of important hecksites, some scheming Foo'Ori Darkassos are known for their abilities to posess mortals to complete secretive missions - if they don't get distracted by any particularly appealing dog food first.
Foo'Ori Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Gala Invader
enemies.description:
A bio-engineered alien soldier, based on nature's perfect predator - the bat. Unfortunately, the aliens who designed this warrior were not informed as to the existence of tennis rackets.
Gala Invader is a group of enemies that appear in Space 54.

enemies.name: Gallo
enemies.description:
Gallo is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. It only appears as a boss and has a chance to drop a Treasure Chest.
Gallo's health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is immune to freeze, instant kill effects and debuffs. Gallo shoots bullets every 0.5 seconds and also has a rotating beam attack, resembling Clock Lancet. It does not deal damage but briefly slows the player upon hit.
There was a Garlic-related bug in a past (1.8.208) version of the game, where Gallo would be knocked back towards the player rather than away when taking damage, resulting in a quick death very reminiscent of the encounter with The Reaper.

enemies.name: Gallotrice
enemies.description:
Gallo had long been haunted by frequent nightmares of being petrified slowly from the feet up to the head, but perhaps more frightening were his dreams of a gigantic predatory chicken. The Gallotrice’s birth was the moment he began to consider that scientific blasphemy as a form of emotional therapy might not be helping anybody.
Gallotrice is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Tiny Bridge, Boss Rash, and Lake Foscari tf. It has a normal variant, which only appears as a normal enemy in Dairy Plant and Gallo Tower, and a boss variant, which appears as a boss in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower and Boss Rash. The gold variant only appears in Tiny Bridge as a normal enemy.
Gallotrice takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant is also resistant to freeze, instant kill and debuffs, and its health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Gambergar
enemies.description:
Unlike their risqué cousins, these palette-swapped scrollkeepers guard a treasure trove of holy scriptures, straight edge lifestyle guides, and family friendly stories full of moral lessons. Their library is roughly ten thousand times less popular than the one with all the cheeky doodles.
Gambergar is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Gamblin
enemies.description:
They'd like you to pick a card, any card. You'll lose no matter your choice, for every single one has been swiped up the Gamblin's moist buttcrack. A laugh at your expense is the cheapest thing Westwoods has to offer.
Gamblin is an enemy that appears in Westwoods and Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Garlic
enemies.description:
Garlic
Garlic is an enemy that appears in Moongolow and Boss Rash. In Moongolow, it appears as both a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Garlic takes reduced knockback. The boss variant's health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Ghiavolo
enemies.description:
Faustian and furious! Low ranking Devils march upon the enemies of Hell armed with infernal pitchforks and an encyclopedic knowledge of the harshest places to shove them.
Ghiavolo (archaic variant of diavolo, the Italian word for devil) is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and Westwoods. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Ghiavolo takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Ghost
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Gallo Tower
enemies.description:
A pure fabrication, the idle fantasy of brains gripped with fever or boredom. There’s simply no such thing as ghosts, and the mere suggestion is to be mocked as ridiculous. These particular apparitions are probably just a trick of the light. Tricks of the light can have hit points too!
Ghost is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, and Gallo Tower, with additional appearances in Moongolow, Whiteout, Astral Stair, Tiny Bridge, and Eudaimonia Machine.
In Inlaid Library, Gallo Tower, Moongolow, Whiteout, Astral Stair, and Tiny Bridge, it appears exclusively as normal enemies. In Mad Forest, it spawns both as a normal enemy and during Ghost Swarm map events. In Boss Rash, it appears only during Ghost Swarm events. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer as a special enemy during the second phase of the stage.
Ghost is semi-resistant to knockback, and the Swarm variant only moves in a fixed direction.

enemies.name: Ghoulette
enemies.description:
The accursed casino has a strict "no rotting body parts" policy. To comply with the flesh code, pestilent ghouls are encased in a gilded carapace that contains their foulness. Most of them work the tables until they go irrevocably mad from no longer being able to scratch their itchy infections.
Ghoulette is an enemy that appears in Westwoods and Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Giant Bat
enemies.description:
Wreathed in shadow, eyes glowing red, such oversized terrors that flap in the night must surely be the sign of a vampire’s approach, yes? Well, no. They’re bats, and nothing more. I’ll admit they’re really bloody big, though.
Giant Bat is a normal enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with additional appearances in Inlaid Library, Boss Rash, Tiny Bridge, and Bat Country.
In Mad Forest, it first appears as a boss and later reappears as a normal enemy in later waves. In Inlaid Library, Bat Country, and Tiny Bridge, it appears only as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a boss.
Giant Bat is semi-resistant to knockback and features a partial hitbox: the upper portion of its wings lacks collision, allowing it to partially pass through walls and other enemies without obstruction.

enemies.name: Giant Enemy Crab
enemies.description:
With a name like theirs, these colossal crustaceans were kind of railroaded into antagonism by a society that didn’t want to understand them. Would it surprise you to learn that Giant Enemy Crabs have an entire culture of their own? Schools of philosophy? Arts and education? Bigotry truly is a sad, sad thing.
Giant Enemy Crab is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss and has a chance to drop a Treasure Chest. Defeating Giant Enemy Crab in Gallo Tower is the requirement for unlocking the stage's hyper mode.

enemies.name: Giant Skeleton
enemies.description:
The answer to the question, “What if skeletons were big?” The Cardinal would ask this question daily to his necromancers in that whiny tone of voice that suggested he really wanted them to make some, but was too embarrassed to outright ask for it. They eventually just made some.
Giant Skeleton is an enemy that appears in The Bone Zone and Boss Rash. In The Bone Zone, it first appears as a normal enemy but later also as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Giant Skeleton takes reduced knockback. The boss variant is also resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Glowing Skeleton
enemies.description:
Glowing Skeleton is an enemy that appears in The Bone Zone. It only appears as a boss.
Glowing Skeleton's health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Gold Jellys
enemies.description:
When a jellyfish eats too much gold, a terrifying transformation takes place whereby it turns from a living jellyfish into a dead jellyfish. Kind of obvious, really. A jellyfish shouldn't be eating any amount of gold.
No idea what these things are, by the way.
Gold Jellys is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Gold Pile
enemies.description:
They resemble a common undead monster but are in fact a hybrid of plant and mineral. While this floral ore is aggressibe, it's worth cultivating in your garden, it'll be the only time you celebrate having Piles.
Gold Pile is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Goldie
enemies.description:
Brownies are unaffected by the Cursino, retaining their free will and physical autonomy. They soon felt left out, however, since losing one's free will and physical autonomy became the hot new trend. They pretend to be as enthralled as everyone else, hoping to stave off the most dreadful curse of all - FOMO.
Goldie is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Hag
enemies.description:
Colder than their own teats, these matriarchs of magic love being ugly, terrifying crones. They genuinely can’t get enough of it. The cackling, the cauldrons, the calling of young maidens “my pretty.” If there’s a stereotype you could attribute to hags and the hag-based lifestyle, these women live it without shame. Good for them.
Hag is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library and Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss and has a chance to drop a Treasure Chest. Killing Hag in Inlaid Library is the requirement for unlocking the stage's hyper mode.
Hag's health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback, and is resistant to freeze, instant kill effects and debuffs.

enemies.name: Happy Molisano
enemies.description:
A Molisano that’s happy.
Happy Molisano is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Happy Molisano cannot move and it can only deal damage by being touched by the player. Though, O'Sole Meeo does not take damage if it touches this enemy.
This enemy gains additional health if the Celestial Dusting interacts with it.

enemies.name: Harzia
enemies.stages: Gallo Tower, Boss Rash, Tiny Bridge, Westwoods, Mazerella
enemies.description:
Brooding in vast nest colonies at the crown of Gallo Tower, these harpies delight in dragging prey high into the sky and ripping them in twain with frighteningly strong talons. To maintain this incredible lower body strength, they never skip leg day.
Harzia is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, Boss Rash, Tiny Bridge, Westwoods, and Mazerella. In Gallo Tower, it appears both as a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss, and in Tiny Bridge, Westwoods, and Mazerella, it only appears as a normal enemy.
Harzia V's movement is fixed on vertical axis. The boss variant's health is based on the player's level, and it is resistant to knockback.

enemies.name: Holy Circuit Creations
enemies.description:
Santa Ladonna's experimental alchemy often has unforeseen side-effects, such as these strange automatons. When one of Ladonna's rituals went awry, she accidentally opened an angelic gate that spewed celestial magic onto a pile of her old VHS tapes, spawning this clanking cadre of retro robots.
Holy Circuit Creations are a group of enemies that appear in Laborratory and Carlo Cart. They appear as normal enemies, bosses, and as parts of map events.
This group consists of four distinct units, each with unique characteristics, which are as follows: ConstableBot, RetroBot, T-DCCC, and ER-2000.

enemies.name: Impefinger
enemies.description:
Mischievous demons who specialize in tomfoolery, shenanigans, and all fourteen disciplines of nonsense. Known for practical jokes, rude limericks, and the occasional cheeky mass murder.
Impefinger is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and Tiny Bridge. It appears as a normal enemy and in the map event, Impefinger Swarm, triggered by stepping on a trap.

enemies.name: Itchiocentaur
enemies.description:
Half-man, half-horse, half-fish, and fully confusing. They rail against the Damp God of the Mermen, choosing instead to spend their time studying the soaked tomes of the Lycaeum and independently developing underwater games.
Itchiocentaur is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Jastor
enemies.description:
Legend has it that a Jastor is born whenever a writer struggles to come up with a pun involving playing cards and clowns. It's such a highly specific scenario that these creatures are exceedingly rare. Anyway, I once saw one kick a cat's head off. True story.
Jastor is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Jellyfish
enemies.description:
Favored pets of the Mermen, their tendency to sting everything within five yards, as well as their complete disregard for potty training, makes them unpopular with literally everybody.
Jellyfish is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Moongolow and Boss Rash. In Dairy Plant, it first appears as part of the Jellyfish Wall and Swarm map events, then as a normal enemy. In Moongolow, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it only appears in Jellyfish Swarms. In Laborratory, it only appears as part of map events.
The event and Moongolow variants have fixed movement and take reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Joyatauro
enemies.description:
A Torino that has evolved through fetamorphosis. Their milk rapidly matures along with them, developing into a potent cheese. Too solid to be extracted through their udders, it must be surgically removed via brie-section.
Joyatauro is an enemy that appears in Mazerella.

enemies.name: Juda R'kasso
enemies.description:
Have you ever read the tragedy of Seiu Darkasso the Sly? It's not a story many who fight the forces of hell would tell you. It's a vampire legend. Seiu was a warlock thrall, one so mighty and sly that they could control blood through occult incantations, manipulating life itself. This warlock had such knowledge of hemomancy, they could even prevent death. though, yes, mostly they use these powers to kill people. Seiu became so mighty, they only thing they feared was losing their sanguinary power. Eventually, of course, they did. They taught their neophyte every dark art they knew. Then the neophyte killed them while they were taking a power nap. Isn't it ironic? Seiu could prevent death, even reverse it, but not for themself. Anyway, Ju Darkasso is the neophyte that killed Seiu Darkasso. Honestly, the less said about this warlock weirdo, the better.
Juda R'kasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Kamaitachi
enemies.description:
Diminutive creature with a colossal temper and known for its cutting wit. Well, just for cutting really. Frankly, its anecdotes are quite boring, but those who point this out tend to have the legs cut out from under them, one way or another.
Kamaitachi is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Kamaitachi takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Kizzune
enemies.description:
An enormous nine-tailed fox capable of summoning dire illusions, the Kizzune is a treacherous adversary that moves with formidable grace and speed, and hits heavily with its flaming tails. The Kizzune is heavily slowed down by snow and hates fire.
Kizzune is an enemy that appears in Whiteout.

enemies.name: Knight of Spades
enemies.description:
Their hearts are harder than diamond, they'll club you to death, and they're not afraid to call a spade a spade. Know when to fold 'em if you hear one shuffle your way, lest it deck you. You'll collapse like a house of dominos.
Knight of Spades is an enemy that appears in Westwoods, as a boss, and Ante Chamber, as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Leda
enemies.description:
Leda is a special enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. Defeating Leda for the first time unlocks her as a playable character.
Unlike most enemies, Leda does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but can be found naturally in Gallo Tower's lower parts, around 43-44 tilesets (map tiles) below the starting area. When approaching her location, the area beyond a certain radius from the player gradually darkens until it becomes black and symbols begin to appear and travel vertically in sine wave pattern. When the player is roughly 90% of the way to her location, the background music also changes. When Leda is killed, the darkness effect vanishes.
Leda has high health and deals high damage but is rather slow. She is immune to knockback, freeze, instant kill effects, such as Pentagram and Rosary, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Levarsee Darkasso
enemies.description:
Greed incarnate, these baneful balls are the final fate of those that succumb to the ancient idiom "eyes bigger than belly". Hoard roast chicken at your peril, lest the foul magics of Room 1665 transform you into an unholy optical orb, a mouthless being cursed with insatiable hunger. Unless you're a cat - cats are immune to this, for whatever reason.
Levarsee Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.
Levarsee Darkassos can also appear if the player has Moonlight Bolero (VI) equipped. A Levarsee Darkasso spawned from this darkana can drop a Dark Treasure Chest once it is defeated.

enemies.name: Levatee Darkasso
enemies.description:
Hell operates on a trickle-down treasurenomics system, and these tiny troublemakers are sick of demonic inequality. The Levatee Darkasso collective have seen right through the unfair structure that constrains them, benefitting the treasure chest hoarding "Bosses" while leaving nothing but a few scant gems for regular enemies - but no longer! These goblinoid thieves are redistributing stolen treasures amongst the demonic masses, so please don't disturb them.
Levatee Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Lionhead
enemies.description:
Some say these many-limbed beasts descended from a great Lord of Hell, whose domain is the healing arts and philosophy. A noble lineage claimed for what was clearly the result of some drunk necromancers and a sewing kit.
Lionhead is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, Boss Rash, and Mazerella. In Inlaid Library, it appears both as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Boss Rash and Mazerella, it only appears as a boss.
Killing 3,000 Lionheads is the requirement for unlocking Yatta Cavallo. This count does not include the unlisted variants of Lionhead.
Lionhead's health is based on the player's level. Its boss variant is also resistant to knockback.

enemies.name: Lizard Pawn
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Carlo Cart, Laborratory, Eudaimonia Machine
enemies.description:
Having grown envious of the mammalian ability to produce milk, the Lizard Folk staged a hostile takeover of the Dairy Plant and seized the means of lactation. Having slain the last of the Milk Mages, these creatures have instigated a campaign of udder despair.
Lizard Pawn is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Carlo Cart, Laborratory, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Dairy Plant, Laborratory, and Carlo Cart, it appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.

enemies.name: Lizard Rook
enemies.description:
Without these stalwart captains, the reptilian forces would never have found the iron discipline and brilliant strategy needed to sneak into a dairy and stab a load of milk-obsessed old men in their sleep.
Lizard Rook is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Carlo Cart, and Laborratory. In Dairy Plant and Carlo Cart, it first appears as a boss then later as a normal enemy. In Laborratory, it only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Lord Ghost
enemies.description:
Some see death as the great equaliser - the inevitable levelling of humanity that strips away rank, wealth, and creed. Those people will still have to report to Lord Ghost in the afterlife, paying spectral tithes to his spectral lordship. Or so it would be, if there were such things as ghosts.
Lord Ghost is an enemy that appears in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Lost Twin
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash, Laborratory, Carlo Cart
enemies.description:
Makes up for the lack of a secondary head by being really, extra, super-duper demonic! They’re not overcompensating, they’re perfectly compensating.
Lost Twin is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, and Laborratory. In Dairy Plant, it appears as a normal enemy, a boss, and as part of map events. In The Bone Zone and Carlo Cart, it appears as a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss if Arcanas are enabled. In Laborratory, it only appears as a boss.
Lost Twin shoots bullets every second, dealing high damage, but cannot move (excluding its racing variants) and is immune to knockback. Additionally, its boss variants' health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: LV128 Golden Bat
enemies.description:
All that glitters is not gold. Sometimes it’s bats. While such a rare creature might seem to herald the coming of something truly momentous, it might surprise you to learn that, despite appearances, they are bats, and nothing more.
LV128 Golden Bat is a special enemy that appears in Green Acres and Bat Country. After entering Green Acres with Hyper Mode and Hurry Mode enabled and travelling far southwest, where the background starts to appear glitched, a large amount of LV128 Golden Bats will spawn instead of the regular enemies. Defeating 128 of these bats, will unlock missingN▯ as a playable character. In Bat Country, it appears both as a normal enemy and a boss.
LV128 Golden Bat takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Madd-Onna
enemies.description:
Despite appearances, a Madd-Onna is absolutely not a ghost, but just an illusion of a very angry woman who had lost every- actually she looks like she's singing now- no she's a dancer- wait is she sifting rice- could someone pause that animation loop please?
Madd-Onna is an enemy that appears in Whiteout. Madd-Onnas are weak to fire.

enemies.name: Mantichana
enemies.description:
Gallo Tower’s early horticultural experiments yielded nought but horrifying mutants. These oversized mantids were bred in Lab 22 and subsequently dumped in the Mad Forest when it became apparent they couldn’t be trained and tasted terrible.
Mantichana is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with additional appearances in Boss Rash and Lake Foscari tf.
In Mad Forest, it first appears as a boss and later reappears as a normal enemy in later waves. In Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a boss. In Lake Foscari, it appears during Circle map events and also as a special enemy that spawns at a specific, fixed location on the map.
Mantichana is semi-resistant to knockback. Its boss and Foscari variants have health that scales with the player's level, with the boss variant also being partially resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Mantichana Idol
enemies.description:
Renardo the Necromancer made a lot of money after selling Edna's genome to Gallo Industries. Pressured to deliver another killing machine, he developed Edna II: Gold Bug. He definitely didn't just nail a cheaply painted plastic head to a dead insect and cash in before anyone noticed.
Mantichana Idol is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Manticore
enemies.description:
A resentful creature with the body of a lion, the tail of a scorpion, and the wings of something with wings. The poison contained within their barbs has a potent hallucinogenic effect, and they like to purposefully sting themselves to maintain their delusions that they can fly.
Manticore is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, Boss Rash, and Mazerella. It has a normal variant, which only appears as a normal enemy in Gallo Tower and Mazerella and a boss variant which appears as a boss in Gallo Tower, Boss Rash, and Mazerella.
Manticore takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant is also resistant to freeze, instant kill and debuffs, and its health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Meat Golem
enemies.description:
Following Gallo Tower’s abandonment by its founder, the scientist-sorcerers that remained were free to satiate their every curiosity, no matter how perverse or unhygienic. The Meat Golem is what happened when “Do No Harm” became “You Do You.”
Meat Golem is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Meat Golem takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Melone
enemies.description:
The Milk Mages of the Dairy Plant devised these constructs as animated pales, for reasons that could only be described as stupid. Completely hollow inside, they can be filled with milk and deliver the cargo to destinations as far away as two miles. The journey takes weeks.
Melone is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Melone takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Menta Elemental
enemies.description:
Sometimes there's so much greed summoned in the world that there aren't enough creatures, dead or alive, to contain it. When that happens, greed soaks into things and brings them to act, even the deep earth itself is raised into berserk elementals. Available in white and blue.
Menta Elemental is an enemy that appears in Whiteout. Menta Elementals are weak to fire.

enemies.name: Merdusa
enemies.description:
Serpentine seductresses whose hypnotic gaze can lure even the most willful of scholars to an early grave.
Merdusa is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library and Boss Rash. In Inlaid Library it appears both as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
The boss variant's health is based on the player's level, and it is resistant to knockback and freeze.

enemies.name: Merman
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Moongolow, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, Laborratory, Eudaimonia Machine
enemies.description:
They reek of fish, drip saltwater everywhere, and talk with really off-putting gurgly voices. Striving to please their Damp God, the Mermen joined with the Lizards in their overthrow of the Dairy Plant.
Merman is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Moongolow, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, Laborratory, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Dairy Plant, Moongolow, Laborratory, and Carlo Cart, it appears as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.
Its boss variant's health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Mignotaur
enemies.description:
While their milk yields are sour, a Mignottaur’s famously tender meat commands a high price at market. Of course, the creatures’ would-be butchers tend to become butchered first.
Mignotaur is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant. It first appears in a Minotaur Rush event and later also as a normal enemy.
Mignotaur takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Milk Elemental
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, Eudaimonia Machine, Mazerella
enemies.description:
Behold, the blasphemy of lactomancy! These homogenized horrors were formulated to pulverize and pasteurize in the name of their intolerant Milk Mages. Any who’ve tried to cream them end up torn in half… and half! This entry has been condensed for those who prefer to skim.
Milk Elemental is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, Eudaimonia Machine, and Mazerella. In Dairy Plant, it first appears as a part of Swarm events, then later as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash and Mazerella, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.
Killing a total of 3,000 Milk Elementals is the requirement for unlocking Bianca Ramba.

enemies.name: Mimic Season One
enemies.description:
Your favorite monsters like you’ve never seen before… BIG!
Mimic Season One is an enemy that appears in Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss.
Mimic Season One takes the appearance of an existing enemy, but has its own stats. Its health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is resistant to freeze and debuffs.

enemies.name: Mimic Season Three
enemies.description:
How are you not impressed by how BIG these monsters are? They’re so BIG!
Mimic Season Three is an enemy that appears in Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss.
Mimic Season Three takes the appearance of an existing enemy, but has its own stats. Its health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is resistant to freeze and debuffs.

enemies.name: Mimic Season Two
enemies.description:
Was the last season of BIG monsters not BIG enough for you? Well, try these BIG monsters on for size! They’re so BIG!
Mimic Season Two is an enemy that appears in Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss.
Mimic Season Two takes the appearance of an existing enemy, but has its own stats. Its health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback and is resistant to freeze and debuffs.

enemies.name: Minotaur
enemies.description:
Yes, they’re bulls. Yes, they’re the source of most of the Dairy Plant’s milk. No, you really shouldn’t ask.
Minotaur is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant and Mazerella. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Minotaur takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Minotaur Boss
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, Mazerella
enemies.description:
Minotaur Boss is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, and Mazerella. In Dairy Plant, it first appears as a boss and later also as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, Carlo Cart, and Mazerella, it only appears as a boss.
Minotaur Boss' health is based on the player's level. The base variant is also resistant to knockback.

enemies.name: Miragellos
enemies.description:
Fleeting visions of ghastly humans from a past far away. Some of them carry ancient memories, and might whisper to you some of the worst things they said when they walked the earth like "you have to pay us 20 gold per install". Today, nobody remembers them.
Miragellos are a group of enemies that appears in Whiteout. Miragellos are weak to fire.

enemies.name: Molisano Grosso
enemies.description:
Molisano Grosso is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Molisano Grosso cannot move.

enemies.name: Moon Atlantean
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, Il Molise, Moongolow, Green Acres, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash
enemies.description:
Powerful guardian of a race long thought extinct. Its mask represents the Moon, bringer of tides, object of mystery, and something to look at when you’re bored at night.
Moon Atlantean is an enemy that appears in all normal, bonus and challenge stages. Unlike most enemies, it does not spawn as part a wave or map event, but spawns upon approaching the Silver Ring, which is one of the hidden stage items unlocked by obtaining the Yellow Sign.

enemies.name: Moon Duck
enemies.description:
Within a generation, duck society has moved with unprecedented speed. Developing technology for locomotion, weaponry and aeronautics, they've investigated some of the most pressing questions in science and the humanities. But the story of the ducks has barely even begun.
Moon Duck is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Moon Rabbit
enemies.description:
All rabbits live on the moon, it is known.
Moon Rabbit is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Moongolow Atlanteans
enemies.description:
Beautiful but baleful, it is unknown whether these delphic entities are true living Atlanteans, magical constructs of a fallen civilization, or something even more curious. They’re not ghosts, so let’s eliminate that nonsense from the possibilities. Their masks are alluring, but none survive the demise of the wearer.
Moongolow Atlanteans are enemies that appears in Moongolow and Abyss Foscari tf. It only appears as a boss.
Moongolow Atlanteans are resistant to freeze, instant kill effects and debuffs and take reduced knockback. When killed, Moongolow Atlantean drops a Golden Egg instead of experience.

enemies.name: Much Much
enemies.description:
Some say they're the cursed souls of business owners who profited greatly by paying their workers a pittance and keeping millions for themselves. After amassing fabulous wealth, they jettisoned their laborers to pocket just a little more for themselves.
This idea has been dismissed as mere myth, for surely no human could be so thoroughly cruel.
Much Much is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Mudman
enemies.description:
The Mudmen of the Mad Forest were once ordinary villagers, but cultural disagreements over whether it was acceptable to cover one’s self in mud and beat passing heroes to death led them to found their own society - a society where it’s acceptable to cover one’s self in mud and beat passing heroes to death.
Mudman is an enemy encountered in Mad Forest, where it appears exclusively as a normal enemy.
Mudman takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Mummy
enemies.description:
Far from true mummies, both spiritually and geographically, their sorcerous creators justify the appropriation of other undead cultures by claiming they just really like the aesthetic and that real mummies should take it as a compliment rather than being so offended all the time.
Mummy is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library and Eudaimonia Machine. In Inlaid Library, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.

enemies.name: Musc Musc
enemies.description:
Cursed by vengeful librarians for the crime of sneezing too loudly, they are perhaps the most pitiable of all wretches. Congealed for all eternity, to slay these victims of disproportionate retribution is a mercy. You’d probably get good karma for doing it if there were such thing as a morality system.
Musc Musc is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant and Boss Rash. In Inlaid Library, it appears both as a normal enemy and a boss. In Dairy Plant, it only appears as an event enemy from a trap. In Boss Rash it only appears as a boss.
Musc Musc's boss variant's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Mushroulette
enemies.description:
When a gambler's too successful for management's liking, they may find themself forcibly frisked by furious forest fungi. The Cursino uses these mushroom bouncers to enforce a cap on winnings.
Mushroulette is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Nesufritto
enemies.description:
The Futile Scribe’s quest for truth ended with nought but babble and madness. Still, there are those that claim to see wisdom in even his most erratic scrawlings. Whether charlatans or fools, it cannot be questioned that, for those with a thought to wield it, there is power in madness.
Nesufritto is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library and Boss Rash. It only appears as a boss and has a chance to drop a Treasure Chest.
Nesufritto's health is based on the player's level. It takes reduced knockback, and is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Nightshade
enemies.description:
Crossbred by a trio of berry farmers, this offshoot of the Garlic is delicious but deadly. The farmers found this out after trying to make berry milk from its poisonous deposits. It was a ridiculous way for them to die.
Nightshade is an enemy that appears in Moongolow and Boss Rash. In Moongolow, it appears as both a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Nightshade takes reduced knockback. The boss variant's health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Non-Giant Enemy Crab
enemies.description:
Did you know that when you put a lot of crabs in a bucket, they actually don’t try to pull each other down to stop any single one from escaping? That was something we projected onto them based on our own cynical and selfish attitudes. Just another example of anti-crab propaganda that your humble author hopes to challenge.
Non-Giant Enemy Crab is an enemy that appears in Moongolow and Boss Rash. In Moongolow, it first appears with its boss variant as a boss and later also as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Non-Giant Enemy Crab's heath is based on the player's level and it moves in a fixed direction across the screen.

enemies.name: Old Molisano
enemies.description:
A Molisano that remembers when you were only yay high.
Old Molisano is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Old Molisano cannot move and it can only deal damage by being touched by the player. Though, O'Sole Meeo does not take damage if it touches this enemy.
This enemy gains additional health if the Celestial Dusting interacts with it.

enemies.name: Olmo
enemies.description:
This species of under-lake lizards once had eyes and a high standing in aquatic society before they somehow saw a strange forbidden sign that forever changed their minds, bodies, and souls. Some say they still search for their excised peepers, warped and enlarged to serve some cosmic force, but I reckon they're just blindly attacking anyone nearby.
Olmo is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Pipeestrello
enemies.description:
The cultural association between bat and vampire stretches back as far as folklore itself. Some claim to have seen the deathly cold visage of a Vampire Lord striding within the swirling maelstrom of these nocturnal nasties, but those people just wanted attention. They’re bats, and nothing more.
Pipeestrello (compare pipistrello, Italian for bat) is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest and Gallo Tower, with additional appearances in Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, Whiteout, Carlo Cart, Bat Country, Tiny Bridge, Ante Chamber, and Eudaimonia Machine.
In Mad Forest, Boss Rash, Bat Country, it appears both as a normal enemy and during the Bat Swarm event. In Gallo Tower and Tiny Bridge, it only spawns as a normal enemy, while in Inlaid Library, it appears exclusively during the Bat Swarm. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by the The Directer as a special enemy during the initial phase of the stage.
There are two boss variants of Pipeestrello: Pipeestrello 4 and Pipeestrello 5
* Pipeestrello 4, also referred to as "Glowing Bat", appears in Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Bat Country, Gallo Tower, Dairy Plant, and Carlo Cart. In Mad Forest and Inlaid Library, spawns both as a regular boss and an Arcana-carrier boss when Arcanas are enabled. In Bat Country, only the regular boss variant appears. In Gallo Tower, Dairy Plant, and Carlo Cart, only the Arcana-carrier boss can appear.
* Pipeestrello 5, also referred to as "Silver Bat", appears only in Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, and Whiteout. It spawns as a regular boss in Mad Forest and Inlaid Library, and also as an Arcana-carrier boss in Whiteout when Arcanas are enabled.
Both boss variants reappear together as regular enemies during later waves in Mad Forest.
The boss variants' health scales with the player's level. The Swarm variant is resistant to defang and moves in a fixed direction.

enemies.name: Poetrait
enemies.description:
Some portraits contain the souls sold by certain witches to obtain eternal youth and health. But let's talk about the Poetrait instead. As Poe becomes ever more aged and garlic scented, this elegant portrait becomes ever younger and smalls increasingly of lavender. Who wouldn't clamour for A Picture of Poe to Display?
Poetrait is an enemy that appears in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Pol.lo Rosso
enemies.description:
Particularly zealous chickens may undergo "Roastification" - plucked, gutted, and cooked with an onion shoven up themselves, alive and aware the entire time.. Posing as tasty floor food, they devour any who eat them from the inside out. Fear the army that marches in your stomach.
Pol.lo Rosso is an enemy that appears in The Coop.

enemies.name: Poltergeist
enemies.description:
There’s a perfectly rational explanation for this. Perhaps these items are the product of a mage’s trickery, or automata dreamed up by Gallo’s gibbering scientists. Maybe each one is filled with a colony of vindictive ants that push them around from inside. Let’s eliminate those possibilities before we mention ghosts.
Poltergeist is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and Cappella Magna. In Gallo Tower the candelabra variants appear in the map event, Poltergeist Roulette, which can be triggered by stepping on a trap. In Cappella Magna, the gem-like variants are spawned as a part of The Trickster's attack pattern.
Poltergeist's health is based on the player's level. If the player gets close enough, it triggers its self-destruct, exploding 2 seconds later for 50 damage. It has no collision and does not take knockback.

enemies.name: Raiju
enemies.description:
A magical critter which descends to the earth inside lightning bolts, hailing from another plane of existence. Where they come from, and how exactly it' s worse place to be than this particular reality, remains a mystery.
Raiju is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Raiju takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Reaper Trainee
enemies.description:
The Interns of Eternity, they’ll reap anything but a paycheck. Really though, isn’t the work experience enough? Many are the apprentices of the Grim Maschera, each hoping to impress Lord Death enough that they may finally harvest souls on commission.
Reaper Trainee is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna, Boss Rash, Tiny Bridge and Eudaimonia Machine. It only appears as a normal enemy in Cappella Magna and Tiny Bridge. It only appears as a boss in Boss Rash. In Eudaimonia Machine it is spawned by The Directer.
Reaper Trainee's health is based on the player's level. It also takes reduced knockback and is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Sad Molisano
enemies.description:
A Molisano that’s sad.
Sad Molisano is an enemy that appears in Il Molise. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Sad Molisano cannot move and it can only deal damage by being touched by the player. Though, O'Sole Meeo does not take damage if it touches this enemy.
This enemy gains additional health if the Celestial Dusting interacts with it.

enemies.name: Scarleton
enemies.description:
Bones made of blood. Or blood made of bones. There’s blood involved somewhere. These rufescent ruffians are out to spill even more of it.
Scarleton is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower and The Bone Zone. In Gallo Tower it first appears as a boss and later also as a normal enemy and in The Bone Zone only as a normal enemy. It cannot drop a Treasure Chest.
Scarleton has 3 lives, meaning that it can resurrect twice. However, if killed by Pentagram, Gorgeous Moon, Rosary or Heaven Sword, it will not resurrect. Each time it dies it drops an Experience Gem.

enemies.name: Scorej-Oni
enemies.description:
Scorej-Oni is a special enemy that appears in Tiny Bridge. Defeating Scorej-Oni for the first time unlocks him as a playable character.
Unlike most enemies, Scorej-Oni does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but can be found naturally far east, around 20 tilesets (map tiles) distance, of the starting area in Tiny Bridge.
Scorej-Oni is resistant to knockback, freeze, instant kill effects, such as Pentagram and Rosary, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Sea Ham
enemies.description:
Though their name suggests they'd make the perfect surf and turf, Sea Hams are too etheral to eat, dissipating into cosmic mist the moment any type of tooth gets near them. Emerging from lakebed trenches, they possess an air of celestial intelligence, despite the way the float mindlessly into masses of projectiles with seemingly no sense of self preservation.
Sea Ham is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Sea Spinach
enemies.description:
Whoever named these moise monstrosities was clearly dehydrated, as they're only found at the bottom of a lake and taste nothing like spinach. These leafy beasts swim around the Lycaeum aimlessly, taking issues with any intruders that disturb their ponderings on dimorphism.
Sea Spinach is an enemy that appears in The Lycaeum.

enemies.name: Serpentvine
enemies.description:
Known among reptilian experts as “the long mover,” they are happy little noodles and very adorable. So that nobody has to feel guilty mowing them down in the tens of thousands, let’s say they really enjoy being mowed down in the tens of thousands.
Serpentvine is an enemy that appears in Moongolow. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Shendi Darkasso
enemies.description:
Once the prophetic terrors of the tides, these primordial shapeshifters were unable to predict their final fate - bewitched by the stone-sorcerer Bomarzo and bound to an eternal battle for Room 1665.
Shendi Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Sig.ra Blu
enemies.description:
Their woeful existences are similar to that of Sig.ra Rossi, but they're significantly more depressed about it.
Sig.ra Blu is an enemy that appears in Moongolow. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Sig.ra Blu ignores collision.

enemies.name: Sig.ra Rossi
enemies.description:
There are works so incomprehensible in theme and meaning as to fracture the reader’s very grasp of reality. Torn from the material world through sheer force of their disbelief in it, these scholarly fools are only one last thought away from volatile oblivion.
Sig.ra Rossi, or Red Shade, is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library. It only appears as a part of the map event, Shade Bomb.
Sig.ra Rossi's health is based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Sinistronz
enemies.description:
Burner of libraries, champion of crashes, hogger of memories, this puzzle box is made to look smart and appealing while it's actually full of half-digested piles of sludge that slowly seep through its surface, making anyone who fell for its enticing presentation and dared to touch it end up sticky, icky, slow, frustrated, bombarded by soliciting attempts, and suddenly be charged hidden fees. Also a necessary evil.
Sinistronz is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Ska'sa Ka'sos
enemies.description:
Ska'sa Ka'sos
Ska'sa Ka'sos is a group of enemies that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Skelegem
enemies.description:
Gem bones, gem bones, gem dry bones! The Experience Gem it's fused with grants enhanced tactical instinct and strategic knowledge. It's smart enough to briefly consider its options before running directly at Survivors.
Skelegem is an enemy from the Call of a Mad Moon (XIII) Darkana that is summoned when the player gets a "four-of-a-kind" roll of Growth.

enemies.name: Skeleton
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, others
enemies.description:
What army of darkness would be complete without skeletons? They are highly disciplined, incredibly vengeful, and very unionized!
Skeleton is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, and The Bone Zone, with additional appearances in Boss Rash and Eudaimonia Machine.
In Mad Forest, Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone, and Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a normal enemy. In Dairy Plant, it spawns both as a normal enemy and during Swarm map events. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer as a special enemy during the second phase of the stage.
Defeating a total of 3,000 Skeletons unlocks the character Mortaccio.

enemies.name: Skeleton Ninja
enemies.description:
These stealth operatives are among the most highly skilled of the undead armies. Their undercover tactics and specialization in sneaking missions are everso slightly undercut by an insistence on wearing brightly colored uniforms.
Skeleton Ninja is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant and The Bone Zone. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Skeleton Panther
enemies.description:
When a panther’s hunger is so great that not even death can satiate its ravening, it returns to feed once more. It doesn’t know that its tummy has long rotted away, however, and is forever confused as to why it can’t keep down its prey.
Skeleton Panther is an enemy that appears in The Bone Zone. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Skeleton Panther takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Skeletone
enemies.description:
More skeleton per skeleton. Skeletons that skeleton harder than the average skeleton. Hobbies include being skeletons, thinking about skeleton stuff, and casual skeletoning. God, the word “skeleton” is weird.
Skeletone is an enemy that appears in The Bone Zone. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Skeletone's health is based on the player's level, and it takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Skelewing
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone
enemies.description:
Fleshless and featherless, the Skelewing flies in the face of all aerodynamic convention. It is theorized that a Skelewing’s extraneous appendages are the grafted remnants of a Skullino’s discarded body.
Skelewing is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone, and Tiny Bridge. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Skelewing takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Sketamari
enemies.description:
Said to be the result of attempts to create a “Bone Moon” for reasons that defy all sense and logic. Driven by hundreds of minds with a singular purpose, it is drawn to places of high skeletal activity with the intent of adding to its chittering mass and growing ever bigger. How would a Bone Moon even work? Pray this horrifying absurdity never comes to pass.
Sketamari is a special enemy that appears in The Bone Zone after obtaining the Yellow Sign. Unlike most enemies, it does not spawn as part a wave or map event, but instead can be found 5 tileset due south of The Bone Zone's center, traveling back and forth horizontally with a range of 5 tilesets in each direction.
