Defeating Sketamari for the first time drops Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane.

enemies.name: Skullino
enemies.description:
Sorcerous experimentation sought to discover if a skeleton, once rendered animate, could toil more efficiently were its head and body split into two separate entities. The answer is no. Of course not. These former farmers, unable to lift the rakes and hoes they so loved, can now only gnash their teeth in eternally silent frustration.
Skullino is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone, Tiny Bridge, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Gallo Tower and The Bone Zone, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.

enemies.name: Skullone
enemies.description:
Nobody knows where these massive laughing skulls first came from. Nobody’s stopped to ask, because they’re massive laughing skulls and they eat horses.
Skullone is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash and Tiny Bridge. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Skullone's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Skulorosso
enemies.description:
Skullinos that longed to be red in the misguided belief they would float faster. Lacking hands of their own, Skulorosso grip brushes between their teeth and paint each other. The last one holding the brush is usually abandoned, and returns to the ranks of the Skullino with a little less faith in the world.
Skulorosso is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Gallo Tower and The Bone Zone, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.

enemies.name: Sneaky Head
enemies.description:
Ranked among the most detested creatures in the land, they find crude sport in pushing unsuspecting victims from ledges when they’re most vulnerable. Faced with an enemy that neither jumps nor climbs, however, they find themselves rather powerless.
Sneaky Head is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, Moongolow, Boss Rash, Tiny Bridge, and Mazerella. In Inlaid Library, it appears as a normal enemy, as a boss and as a part of Medusa Swarm and Medusa Wall map events. In Moongolow, Tiny Bridge, and Mazerella, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Sneaky Head's moves horizontally across the screen in a wavy pattern, instead of homing to the player. The unit has a "fast" variant, which has higher movespeed. The "aggro" and boss variants have normal movespeed, and do not have the fixed movement restriction, chasing the player like most other enemies. Its boss variant's health is based on the player's level, and it takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Space Ant Onion
enemies.description:
The Space Ants build complex networks of tunnels within planets and moons, lit by crystals, oxygenated by mushroom colonies. However, their perfect and orderly society has done little to dissuade other beings from dubbing them the basement dwelling losers of the cosmos.
Space Ant Onion is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Space Hunter
enemies.description:
What is the most dangerous game? This interstellar apex predator has scoured space and time to discover the answer to this question, hunting elk, alien mega-bears, and even defeating several futuristic virtual hunting simulators. Now, they've determined that the most dangerous game of all is hunting vampire hunters in an abandoned alchemist's lab.
Space Hunter is an enemy that appears in Laborratory.

enemies.name: Space Pickle
enemies.description:
Ancient scrolls discovered in the deep subterranean temples of their home planet foretold that these beings would conquer the world. They did not, in fact, conquer anywhere, but got chased away by an astronomer wielding a blowtorch.
Space Pickle is an enemy that appears in Space 54.

enemies.name: Sphon'Dato Darkasso
enemies.description:
Sphon'Dato Darkasso
Sphon'Dato Darkasso is an enemy that appears in Room 1665.

enemies.name: Squillers
enemies.description:
The squirrels of Westwoods knew nothing of money before the Cursino took hold. Now they hoard cash over cashews, demolishing their cute hovels to live in canopy penthouses. This newfound avarice hastened the forest's fall to gentreefication.
Squillers is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Stage Killer
enemies.description:
“How many heroes have fallen now? How many campaigns have blazed a trail to power unimaginable and ended with a weak, pathetic bleating? Fight us if you will, forget us if you can. You soon shall be just another one of us. Defeated.”
Stage Killer is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Killing 6,000 Stage Killers is the requirement for unlocking Sir Ambrojoe.
Stage Killer's health is based on the player's level.
It resembles one of sixteen playable characters, and shares its appearance with said playable character put in Holy Forbidden.

enemies.name: Succubus
enemies.description:
Succubus
Succubus is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Boss Rash. In Cappella Magna it first appears as a normal enemy and later also as a boss. In Boss Rash it only appears as a boss.
Succubus takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant's health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Sun Atlantean
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, Il Molise, Moongolow, Green Acres, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash
enemies.description:
Powerful guardian of a race long thought extinct. Its mask represents the Sun, giver of life, subject of worship, and friend to ice cream sellers everywhere.
Sun Atlantean is an enemy that appears in all normal, bonus and challenge stages. Unlike most enemies, it does not spawn as part a wave or map event, but spawns upon approaching the Gold Ring, which is one of the hidden stage items unlocked by obtaining the Yellow Sign.

enemies.name: Sword Guardian
enemies.resistances: Freeze, Instant kill, Debuff (boss variant only)
enemies.description:
They are not guardians that carry swords, but rather guardians of their swords. They jealously attack anybody who so much as looks at their mighty blades, which is practically everybody because look at the size of ‘em!
Sword Guardian is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant and Boss Rash. It appears both as a normal enemy and boss.
Sword Guardian takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant's health is also based on the player's level and is resistant to freeze, instant kill effects, and debuffs.
Defeating the Sword Guardian boss that appears at 25:00 in Dairy Plant unlocks the hyper mode for that stage.

enemies.name: Swordian
enemies.skills: HP x Level, Fixed Direction, Floaty
enemies.description:
Swordian is an enemy that appears in Tiny Bridge. It first appears as a boss and later also normal enemy and in the Monster Rain map event.
Swordian takes reduced knockback. Its boss variants' health is also based on the player's level.

enemies.name: Testa di Mano
enemies.description:
Incredibly self-conscious about their appearance due to a glaringly obvious abnormality. If you’re unfortunate enough to meet one, on no account should you ever point out they’re not wearing shoes.
Testa di Mano is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library, Gallo Tower, and Eudaimonia Machine. In Inlaid Library and Gallo Tower, it only appears as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer.
Testa di Mano takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Tetrabrachia
enemies.description:
Beautiful and deadly warriors, the Tetrabrachia act as footsoldiers for Cappella Magna’s pious ruling class. They claim they can never be ambushed or surprised in a fight, because four-armed is forewarned.
Tetrabrachia is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Tiny Bridge. It only appears as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: The Blinder
The Directer
enemies.resistances: Freeze, Rosary, Debuff, Instant kill, Defang
enemies.description:
Boundless gifts. Sights beyond reality. Glimpses of the unthinkable.
The Directer is a special boss enemy that appears in Eudaimonia Machine, and is the final boss of Vampire Survivors.
The Directer cannot be damaged. It takes no knockback and is resistant to freeze, instant kill effects, and debuffs.

enemies.name: The Drowner
enemies.stages: Gallo Tower, The Bone Zone, Cappella Magna, The Lycaeum, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart

enemies.name: The Ender
enemies.description:
When the power of friendship goes planet. The ultimate personification of oblivion, The Ender encapsulates all aspects of true despair - Death, Madness, Obsession, Deceit, and Being Wet. Its arrival signifies true futility, a final warning to those who’ve embarked on a doomed quest and refuse to understand that what they seek is not here, in this world or the next.
The Ender is a special boss enemy that appears in Cappella Magna and Boss Rash. It appears to be an amalgamation of The Reaper, The Trickster, The Stalker, The Drowner, and The Maddener merged into one.
It acts as the final enemy in Cappella Magna, spawning shortly after the player reaches the 30:00 mark until it is defeated. Defeating it unlocks Game Killer (0), and also drops the Great Gospel on the floor to be picked up. In Boss Rash, it spawns as a wave boss. The Yellow Sign must be collected before The Ender will spawn.
The Ender's health is based on the player's level and it is resistant to knockback, freeze, instant kill and debuffs. It also has a shield that temporarily absorbs damage.

enemies.name: The Maddener
enemies.stages: Holy Forbidden, Cappella Magna, Boss Rash, Carlo Cart
enemies.description:
A Reaper whose true form lies beyond the edge of sanity. Bearing the power to alter reality itself, it exists to confuse and disorient, and feeds on the mental anguish inspired in its victims. When robbed of its ability to beguile, however, it falls prey to the very fear and bewilderment it causes in others, its very sense of self overridden by sheer panic.
The Maddener is an enemy that makes its first appearance in Holy Forbidden as a special enemy, and in Cappella Magna, Boss Rash, and Carlo Cart as an event or boss enemy.
Maddener's health is based on the player's level. It is immune to knockback, freeze, instant kill and debuffs.

enemies.name: The Reaper
enemies.stages: All normal, challenge and bonus stages
enemies.description:
The Reaper
The Reaper is an enemy that spawns once every minute after the time limit of a stage has been reached, unless endless mode has been turned on. In Eudaimonia Machine, a more vulnerable variant of the Reaper is summoned by The Directer.

enemies.name: The Stalker
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Cappella Magna, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash

enemies.name: The Trickster
enemies.stages: Inlaid Library, Cappella Magna, Carlo Cart
enemies.description:
A Reaper that specializes in murder by illusion. Treasure hunters especially fall foul of the Trickster’s deadly jokes, eagerly pocketing the gems it manifests and learning all too late that they’ve stuffed their pantaloons with supernatural explosives. Loves to be the death of the party.
The Trickster is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna, Inlaid Library, Boss Rash, and Carlo Cart.
Trickster's health is based on the player's level, and it is immune to knockback, freeze, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Toll
enemies.description:
Any adventurer foolish enough to desire entry into Westwoods has got to pay the troll toll to get in. At least, that's what the naive Toll seems to think. It's a forest, you can just walk into it from any direction.
Toll is an enemy that appears in Westwoods.

enemies.name: Torino
enemies.description:
Torinos come from a pocket dimension famous for its wildlife tours, a sort of "safari" zone if you will. The Milk Mages tried to catch them all after learning how delectable their creamy drippings were. Many instead caught a pair of horns with their all-too fragile ribcages.
Torino is an enemy that appears in Mazerella.

enemies.name: Tri-Anchors
enemies.description:
Its father was a great beast that arrived to this world within the belly of a meteor. Its mother was a fish. Each head has its own personality, core values, and political affiliation.
Tri-Anchors is an enemy that appears in Boss Rash and Carlo Cart. In Boss Rash, it appears both as a boss and a normal enemy. In Carlo Cart, it appears as a special enemy, guarding the coffin of the secret character found on the stage.
Tri-Anchors' health is based on the player's level. It is immune to knockback, freeze, debuffs, and defang. It also has no collision, allowing it to pass through walls and other enemies.

enemies.name: Tri-Blunder
enemies.description:
Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results. Unless you ask for the same thing 13 times, then you know what happens? Mecha-Gyorunton!
Tri-Blunder is an enemy that appears in Laborratory. It appears as a normal enemy, a boss, and as part of map events.
Tri-Blunder is immune to knockback, freeze, debuffs, and defang. Its boss variants' health is based on the player's level. Furthermore, the base and boss variants do not collide with walls or other enemies.

enemies.name: Trinacria
enemies.description:
Created to reach the stars, but she's gone much, much farther than that. She tore a hole in our universe, a gateway to another dimension. A dimension of pure chaos. Pure… evil. Look at her, isn't she beautiful?
Trinacria is an enemy that appears in Cappella Magna, Boss Rash, Moongolow and Holy Forbidden. In Cappella Magna, it first appears as a boss and later also as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash and Moongolow, it only appears as a boss. In Holy Forbidden, it appears as an event enemy, a large amount of them being spawned as the player approaches the end of the corridor.
Defeating Trinacria (boss) in Cappella Magna is the requirement for unlocking the stage's hyper mode.
Trinacria takes reduced knockback. Its unlisted variants' health is also based on the player's level and they are resistant to freeze, instant kill and debuffs.

enemies.name: Tritont
enemies.stages: Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, The Lycaeum
enemies.resistances: Freeze, Instant kill, Debuff (boss variant only)
enemies.description:
Mighty warriors of the oceanic depths, Tritonts are famed for their stunning good looks and charisma. Their enigmatic haircare routine is one of the most treasured secrets in all the world, with entire nations having fallen in violent pursuit of the knowledge.
Tritont is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant, Boss Rash, and The Lycaeum. In Dairy Plant, it first appears as a boss, then later as a normal enemy. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss. In The Lycaeum, it only appears as a normal enemy.
Tritont takes reduced knockback. Its boss variant's health is also based on the player's level and is resistant to freeze, instant kill effects, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Twin Demons
enemies.description:
A demonic variant of the Twin Snakes, hence the name Twin Demons. You can tell they’re demonic because they’re a bit red. Classic case of demonicism right there.
Twin Demons is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant and The Bone Zone. It shoots bullets every 1.5 seconds, dealing high damage, but cannot move. It appears as a normal enemy and as a part of a map event, Pile Assault.

enemies.name: Twin Skulls
enemies.description:
After a pair of Twin Snakes die, their skeletal remains may mysteriously reawaken. They’re generally not pleased with this, because being a Twin Snake wasn’t particularly thrilling to begin with. They look happy though, so at least they don’t bring the mood down.
Twin Skulls is an enemy that appears in The Bone Zone. It appears as a normal enemy and as a part of a map event, Skull Pile Pile.
Twin Skulls shoots bullets, once every second, dealing high damage, but cannot move. It takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Twin Snakes
enemies.description:
While these sinister visages think independently, their shared digestive system necessitates a symbiotic reliance upon each other. One head can only consume solids. The other, only liquids.
Twin Snakes is an enemy that appears in Dairy Plant. It first appears as a part of a map event, Pile Assault, and later also as a normal enemy. It shoots bullets every 2 seconds, dealing high damage, but cannot move.

enemies.name: Undead Eyes
enemies.description:
Undead Eyes is a special enemy that appears in inverse Inlaid Library.
Unlike most enemies, Undead Eyes does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but spawns under certain conditions in inverted Inlaid Library after obtaining Yellow Sign and Greatest Jubilee.
Undead Eyes is resistant to knockback.

enemies.name: Undead Head
enemies.description:
Undead Head is a special enemy that appears in inverse Inlaid Library.
Unlike most enemies, Undead Head does not spawn as a part a wave or map event, but spawns under certain conditions in inverted Inlaid Library after obtaining Yellow Sign and Greatest Jubilee.
Undead Head is resistant to knockback.

enemies.name: Undead Mage
enemies.description:
Boys possessed of prodigious magical talent are regularly sent to Gallo’s esteemed Academy of Alchemia. Here, they hone their powers, learn devastating spells, and perfect the art of lacemaking.
Undead Mage is an enemy that appears in Gallo Tower. It appears as a normal enemy, a boss and part of the map event, Pile Assault.
Undead Mage shoots bullets every 2 seconds and takes no knockback.

enemies.name: Undead Sassy Witch
enemies.description:
Giovanna]] resented being assigned Mage at birth, and proudly took up the way of the broom and pointed hat. Her sisters, who claim they want to “protect witches’ spaces,” have sworn to oppose her and all who fight by her side. Maybe one day they’ll accept that anybody can be a Sassy Witch if they truly want to be.
Undead Sassy Witch is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library and Boss Rash. In Inlaid Library, it appears both as a normal enemy and as a boss. In Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss.
Undead Sassy Witch takes increased knockback. The boss variant instead takes reduced knockback, its health is based on the player's level and it is resistant to freeze.

enemies.name: Undead Stars
enemies.description:
In this astral plane, the fire of the Infernas reaches into the minds of cosmic entities, driving them into a frenzy of harmonic discord. A veritable disco inferno, if you will. You won't? That's very fair. Strike that bit from the record.
Undead Stars is a group of enemies that appear in Astral Stair.

enemies.name: Undead Witch
enemies.description:
The Sisterhood of Witches keeps secrets that could topple dynasties. Four fifths of these secrets are sex scandals. The influx of noble bribe money ensures that no witch goes without a fancy hat.
Undead Witch is an enemy that appears in Inlaid Library. It only appears as a normal enemy.
Undead Witch takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Unknown
enemies.description:
I can’t see them, but they see me. I can feel them. Watching. Always watching. The pressure of their gaze pushes down on me like earth on the grave. Who’s paranoid? Me? I’m not paranoid. You’re paranoid. Who’s looking at me from behind those lidless orbs?
Unknown is an enemy that appears in Moongolow, Cappella Magna, and Boss Rash. In Moongolow, it appears during the Lunar eclipse event, first as a boss and later also as a normal enemy. In Cappella Magna and Boss Rash, it only appears as a boss. When it appears as a boss it can drop a Treasure Chest.
Unknown's health is based on the player's level and it takes reduced knockback. It also does not collide with other enemies and is resistant to freeze, instant kill, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Valentine
enemies.description:
The heart of the cards, unless that phrase is trademarked, in which case it's the primary circulatory organ of 52 rectangular pieces of polyethylene-coated paper commonly used in games such as poker, blackjack, and garlic rummy.
Valentine is an enemy that appears in Westwoods. It appears as a boss in the first wave that it appears before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Venus
enemies.description:
The center of this flower possesses an attractive feminine form, but it’s little more than a lure, cleverly folded petals puppeted by the carnivorous flower that houses it. Those prone to thinking with their britches are likely to become easy prey.
Venus is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with an additional appearance in Boss Rash.
In Mad Forest, it first appears as a boss and later reappears as a normal enemy in later waves. In Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a boss.
Venus is semi-resistant to knockback. Its boss variant has health that scales with the player's level and is partially resistant to freeze.
Defeating the Giant Blue Venus that spawns at 25:00 mark in Mad Forest for the first time unlocks the stage's Hyper Mode.

enemies.name: Volcano Atlantean
enemies.stages: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappella Magna, Il Molise, Moongolow, Green Acres, The Bone Zone, Boss Rash
enemies.description:
Powerful guardian of a race long thought extinct. Its mask represents fire and fury, the rage of the natural world, seething heat and opposition to a man named Joe.
Volcano Atlantean is an enemy that appears in all normal, bonus and challenge stages. Unlike most enemies, it does not spawn as part a wave or map event, but spawns upon approaching the Metaglio Right, which is one of the hidden stage items unlocked by obtaining the Yellow Sign.

enemies.name: Werewolf
enemies.description:
Said to have evolved from verminous creatures that flocked from a world trapped in time. Their lupine nature has been called into question, but if you ask for their opinion, they’ll tear you to shreds with a most uncommon brutality. They must be sensitive about it.
Werewolf is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with additional appearances in Dairy Plant and Boss Rash.
In Mad Forest, it appears as both a normal enemy and a boss. In Boss Rash, it appears exclusively as a boss. In Dairy Plant, it spawns as a special enemy after collecting the Cheese pickup on the stage.
Werewolf takes reduced knockback. It has two distinct boss variants: Boss 1, also known as "Giant Werewolf", whose health scales with the player's level, and Boss 2, also known as "Colossal Werewolf", which does not.

enemies.name: Zombie
enemies.description:
“Why simply work the smallfolk to death? Work them beyond it!” This, the Cardinal’s necromancers laughed as they turned to the grave for a cheap alternative to labor that needed rest and food. Sadly for them, while their new workforce slept not, feeding was a whole other matter.
Zombie is an enemy primarily encountered in Mad Forest, with an additional appearance in Eudaimonia Machine.
In Mad Forest, it appears exclusively as a normal enemy. In Eudaimonia Machine, it is summoned by The Directer as a special enemy during the second phase of the stage.
Zombie takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Big Blind
enemies.description:
The bats upped the ante with this one! Like a Small Blind, only bigger and therefore much more dangerous. Unfortunately, you can't choose to skip it in exchange for some bonus rewards so your only choice is to survive!
Big Blind is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Blue Venus
enemies.description:
Jesters who tell particularly risqué jokes are sometimes punished by being fed to carnivorous plants. That's what you get for being a blue joker.
Blue Venus is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Crimson Heart
enemies.description:
A weapon to surpass the Boss Blind, it's the BIG Boss Blind! She is no joke, which is a really great joke if you get the joke. Take heart when the chips are down, and poke her face with whatever you've got to hand. Survive this showdown or we'll all be as extinct as the gros michel!
Crimson Heart is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Flower Pot
enemies.description:
Capable of adding a X3 Mult to their damage, but since multiplier mechanics don't work in real life, the powers of the flowers are absolutely meaningless.
Flower Pot is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Jimbats
enemies.description:
Sometimes called Batlatros, they're considered pests by the citizens of Balatropolis for getting guanatro on everything. To the casual observer, their heads ever so slightly resemble that of a human clown's, but rest assured they're bats and nothing more.
Jimbats is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Moonlover
enemies.description:
Cursed card sharks who transform into wolves under a full house. Known for being greedy, wrathful, lusty, and gluttonous. The hats may make them look friendly, but they're worn purely for brand awareness.
Moonlover is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Mr Bones
enemies.description:
Skeletal jokers who have had their last laugh. It is said they have the power to protect a comedian from dying on stage if at least 25% of their jokes are funny.
Mr Bones is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Playing Mantis
enemies.description:
If you challenge these jovial insects to a game of cards, they have to accept, such is the compulsion of the playing mantis. Just make sure to let them win, because those claws can cut more than cards.
Playing Mantis is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber. It first appears as a boss in that stage twice, before becoming a normal enemy in later waves.

enemies.name: Small Blind
enemies.description:
It seems the pippistrellos of the Mad Forest took exception to the phrase "blind as a bat" and are using this Blind AS a bat with which to bludgeon us all. It's just a small one though, so it's nothing to worry about.
Small Blind is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Spectral Joker
enemies.description:
Everybody knows Spectral Cards aren't real. The very idea that cards can become ghosts really highlights how stupid the ghost truther movement is. Spectral Cards are a hoax created by jokers in cheap Halloween costumes that aren't fooling anyone.
Spectral Joker is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: The Manacle
enemies.description:
Don't touch it or it'll bite a finger off, inflicting minus one to your hand size. Can you believe this bestiary is free? Funny AND well researched, what a bargain!
Anyway, I think this monster is based on something from a game called Clown Cards.
The Manacle is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: The Ox
enemies.description:
It can steal the money right out of your pocket, which the bats spend on comic books, cola cubes, and offshore investments. Due to its thieving nature, it is colloquially known as the "Robs You" Blind.
The Ox is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: The Wall
enemies.description:
A Blind that comes in extra large, which is great news for the plus size market. Nothing fancy about this one, it can simply take loads and loads of damage. You'd think you could just target the bats so they drop it, but they don't teach target selection in Vampire Survivor school.
The Wall is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Zombalatro
enemies.description:
They got a raw deal when the Reaper called their number, shuffling off this mortal coil in dire straights. Rather than just lay down, they reraised and now openly limp in search of guts to open with their fouled hands.
I bet this entry polarizes readers who've hit the limit on wordplay, but I think I aced it.
Zombalatro is an enemy that appears in Ante Chamber.

enemies.name: Alraune
enemies.description:
A naughty veggie boy with a penchant for nudging things. He's caused real horticultural havoc in the Great Tree, and likes to fiddle around in your garden while poking potholes, chomping on grass, and tickling spuds like the cheeky little spud tickler he is.
Alraune is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Anti-Ant
enemies.description:
Their name isn't mere wordplay (heavens forbid we start doing puns) but an allusion to the very real hatred they feel towards ants. Anti-Ants hate the "mushroomy" Naml of Cordycep, coined the cruel moniker "Lesser Ants" for those in Wichdom Pulchra, and even found a way to travel through the Junction to insult the esoteric Space Ants.. They claim they're not ant racists, they just want Anti-Ant Land for the Anti-Ants. They're total ant racists, and frankly their views on caterpillars are pretty disgusting too.
Anti-Ant is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a normal enemy and a boss.

enemies.name: Boar Infantry
enemies.description:
Boar Infantry and their redder cousins War Hogs make for an ordered and effective military force known for rudely interrupting adventurers from Pulchra to Yomi with meaty counterattacks. Their fronts are heavily armored, but if you think the hind portions are vulnerable, you aren't prepared for the natural defenses they can deploy at a moment's notice.
Boar Infantry is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Calamity
enemies.description:
Calamities only feel the opposite of the expression carved into their faces, except every Tuesday when the emotion matches the appearance. Unless of course it happens to be the 12th or 22nd of the month, in which case they’re slightly to the emotional right of how they look.
Said to be the elemental manifestation of the malign influence spreading across Pulchra and Beyond, saving the witchdom might require a mystical therapy session to bring them back to neutrality.
Calamity is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Cursed Monarch
enemies.description:
Cursed Monarch is a boss enemy that can be encountered at 25:00 in any part of the Emerald Diorama stage.
If the player manages to kill this boss, they will be able to unlock the hyper mode for Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Decobat
enemies.description:
A Decobat's beak can shatter bones and puncture full plate armor with its Interrupting Tackle technique, preying on the passenger ships of Mare Nostrum and other un-ceilinged places. Even scarier, it can be used to gossip about other Decobats, which these meddling little scandal merchants do all the time. Each monster is involved in at least three slander lawsuits.
Decobat is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Divine Wood Spirit
enemies.description:
Spirits of the wood known for their divinity. The wood is what they are spirits of, and divine is the trait by which these spirits are known. Not to be confused with Infernal Bush Spookies. Ask yourself if it is in a wood, is a spirit, and is divine - if the answer to all three "yes" then it's probably a Divine Wood Spirit.. The stunning Brilliance of the Divine Spirit should spell the end for many adventurers through the Emerald Dream, but fortunately they're more interested in flying about and screaming than they are with eating any nearly-defeated prey.
Divine Wood Spirit is an enemy that appears in Miyako City as a part of the Emerald Diorama DLC. It drops Pummarola on death.
Defeating it in Inverse mode unlocks Kugutsu as playable character.

enemies.name: Earth Dragon
enemies.description:
Named not just for their elemental affinity, but because seeing one makes you soil yourself. A single scale is equal in weight to a large boulder, which makes its ability to fly quite baffling, not to mention terrifying during molting season.. In the aftermath of the War at Brighthome at least one Earth Dragon has taken to peaceful gardening, using its Gliding Spikes technique to more effectively plant rows of beautiful flowers and crops.
Earth Dragon is an enemy that appears in in Witchdom Pulchra as a part of the Emerald Diorama DLC. It drops Glaive on death.
Defeating it in Inverse Emerald Diorama as Tsunanori Mido unlocks Lita Caryx as playable character.

enemies.name: Failinis
enemies.description:
Dangerous dog-beasts believed to originate from Pulchra are usually called either Failinis or Barghests, though they're clearly different colours and have very little else in common. Barghest specimens studied in Delta Base are well known by analysts for their propensity to tear anything left unattended to shreds with their fearsome fangs, and for tearing up the discotheque with their Azure Dance.. Failinis, on the other hand, once were genies who became infernal meanies. They love to eat paninis and get wasted on martinis. As demons go they're teeny and they look cute in a beanie, but don't assume they're weenies, they still tempted Paganini. These claims were made by a somewhat wobbly citizen after they were unfrozen in Grelon, so they might not be entirely accurate.
Failinis is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Forest Hermit
enemies.description:
Ancient legends from the Witchdom of Pulchra claim these are former humans who opted out of society to live free and lawless. Their love of liberty is so extreme that merely implying they can't do something will be met with angry insistences on doing that thing, which is why over 200 Hermits a year die eating poison berries, often using their famed "Lick and Cut" technique. A belief in freedom so zealous as to be indistinguishable from chains.
Forest Hermit is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Golden Baum
enemies.description:
Often referenced by the avant-garde poets of Avalon, Baums are sensitive about a spurious verse suggesting they're the blasphemous result of an alchemist eating gummy bears too close to an experiment. It's suggested you don't refer to one as a "Horribo" unless you want a furious glob of understandably indignant gelatin to deal with.
Golden Baum is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It first appears as a boss before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Iron Maiden
enemies.description:
These quasi-angelic spirits are thought to be manifestations of maleficent thoughts, born to constrain others with their Freezing Blaster. Iron Maidens coalesce occasionally amongst the dour towers of Yomi, though one appeared to seal away the power of the Final Emperor in Grelon, probably out of spite.. As it turns out, most folk's nasty notions take on the physical form of a gigantic horse-angle-thing with gorgeous flowing heair and a set of floating wings, but I'm not a psychologist or a theologist so I couldn't tell you what that means.
Iron Maiden is an enemy that appears in Avalon as a part of the Emerald Diorama DLC. It drops Khukuri on death.
Defeating it in Inverse Emerald Diorama as Ameya Aisling unlocks Macha Alter Ego as a playable character.

enemies.name: Kelpie
enemies.description:
Though sailors on the high seas of Mare Nostrum refer to these umimaginatively as "Blue Drakes", I believe this may be a distant relative of the Foscaranm Kelpie, which I've classified as the Webbed Longneck-Goofbeak Kelpie. Its unusual appearance may lead bestiary authors to underestimate it, perhaps even taunt it during a field study, only to regret doing so when one of the things barfs up its Putrid Breath and stuns their sister with its stench.
Kelpie is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Living Anguish
enemies.description:
Constantine, is this fate? Or just destiny? What lies Beyond, unknowable, but forced to threaten the Conjoined Worlds. Remember the forbidden lyrics, find your voice, give us one last song and dance.
Living Anguish is an enemy that appears in Providence as a part of the Emerald Diorama DLC. It drops Skull O'Maniac on death.

enemies.name: Maggot Ball
enemies.description:
There's nothing outwardly maggoty about these flapping facial freaks, which makes one wonder. why are they called that? Are the pirates of Mare Nostrum just having a laugh with these names? Oh gods. they're not inside them, are they? I swear, if these things are supposed to be packed with maggots and they're grinning about it, I quit. I quit monsters forever.
Maggot Ball is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Malevolent Door Spirit
enemies.description:
Malevolent Door Spirit
Malevolent Door Spirit is an enemy that appears in Grelon. It drops Flamberge on death.
Defeating it in Inverse Emerald Diorama as either Bonnie Blair or Formina Franklyn unlocks Final Emperor as a playable character.

enemies.name: Moch
enemies.description:
Despite looking like something you'd catch and fight other monsters with, this deciduous decimator's giant crushing hands make it the most deadly palm plant in existence. At first nobody took it seriously, as warnings about an outbreak of Moch battles were perilously misunderstood. Now, they're known for their wandering nature, strange life cycle, and their ironically named Felling Blow deployed against daring lumberjacks.
Moch is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Psychic Ogre
enemies.description:
Colloquially known as the Psychlops but you probably shouldn't tell them that. Advanced mental abilities allow them to perceive so much more than depth, having skipped the first two eyes and jumped straight to the third. Fiendish studies of Psychic Ogre specimens haven't gone far, as their Mind Blast tends to make any potential Delta Base investigators forget anything they've learned, as well as what they had for breakfast.
Psychic Ogre is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Rana Combatant
enemies.description:
Amphibious conquerors who wish to be feared but cannot conquer the universal truth that frogs are funny. Rana Combatants have proved powerful largely as their enemies are often too busy laughing to fight back. Their Amphibian Assault techniques have conquered foes and left their summoners consumed by fits of laughter in Grelon and Mare Nostrum, leaving the froggy fighters with a frquent confused malaise. If they only wished to make the world a happier place, the Rana would want for nothing.
Rana Combatant is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Rascal
enemies.description:
Speculated to have evolved from a race of talkative furry creatures that humans kept as pets in the distant past of the 1990s. Biologists dismiss this idea as pure fantasy because stupid science has to ruin everything with stupid facts and stupid research. Fortunately, these furry foes are experts in Metal magic and making their allies move faster, all the better to smash up the labs of Delta Base.
Rascal is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Skeleton from Beyond
enemies.description:
Though the bony undead of Mare Nostrum haven't figured out how to unionize yet, they do have a piratical system of proto-socialism that seems like it would work quite well - if they had any method of communicating with one another beyond rattling their ribcages and dancing.. Delta Base researchers have observed that the most proficient Skeleton Dancers can deploy a Devilish Smash ability, making them particularly good at escaping high-tech containment systems to hold impromptu breakdance competitions.
Skeleton from Beyond is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a normal enemy and a boss.

enemies.name: Skydiver
enemies.description:
Fearsome beasts with the wings of a bird, the talons of a bird, and the taxonomic designation of a bird. Sure, a giant bird might not be the most exciting monster, but I once saw one strangle an ape with its Feather Shot. Yes, strangle. Do you know how determined a bird has to be in order to strangle an ape? Using only its feathers? Terrifying.
Skydiver is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Specter Head
enemies.description: Specter Head is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama.

enemies.name: Specter of Iwanaga-hime
enemies.description:
Delta Base boffins have found no evidence of the inscrutable Specters obeying any form of speed limit, and plenty of evidence that those spiky wheels aren't just for show, especially when use in conjunction with a devastating Axel Turn. Fast, appearently immortal, and a big fan of throwing exploding heads at its enemies, the Specter of Iwanaga-hime ranks highly amongst the forces of Chaos in Brighthome. Its subordinates often mishear its orders as it speeds around, but that just ensures truly chaotic operations.
Specter of Iwanaga-hime is an enemy that appears in Yomi as a part of the Emerald Diorama DLC. It drops Bullova on death.
Defeating it in Inverse Emerald Diorama as Siugnas unlocks Dolores as playable character.

enemies.name: Werewolf from Beyond
enemies.description:
Bestiary writers being paid per entry has nothing to do with how many werewolves are listed in the average creature compendium. It's simply important to categorize every werewolf from every possible reality (including Yomi), for reasons far too complicated to discuss. Anyway, this one has brown knickers on.
Werewolf from Beyond is an enemy that appears in Emerald Diorama. It appears as a boss before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Brainoid
enemies.description:
These aliens are something of a biological oxymoron. They're so lazy they developed massive brains for the sole purpose of automating every aspect of their lives. After this herculean feat of effort they spent the following few millennia wallowing in inactivity.
Brainoid is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Frijjitello
enemies.description:
Smart, mechanically adept, and devastatingly sarcastic, these aliens are always the preferred hire for starship engineering crew. All their instructions drip with sardonic irony, so it's best to do the opposite of whatever they say.
Frijjitello is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: G062T
enemies.description:
A venerable old battle-bot with a legacy of service stretching back decades. Unfortunately it's friendly fire protocols have deprecated, so rampaging battle groups of the old machines terrorise abandoned worlds to this day.
G062T is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Martian Face
enemies.description:
Did you know that there is a face on Mars? Well, there's actually more than one, and they're all furious. Some suspect this murderous rage is an attempt to make Mars as inhospitable as possible in response to hearing industrialist fantasies of colonising the red planet, but the language barrier makes it difficult to tell for sure.
Martian Face is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica. It first appears as a boss before appearing as a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Meat Bean
enemies.description:
The repulsive meaty effluence of a vicious, yet very cute, murderous monster. It's hotly debated whether these lumps of animate offal are some sort of offspring, or merely a biological defence mechanism.
Meat Bean is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Mocholo
enemies.description:
Part of a twin pair of species that exist in a state of mutually beneficial symbiosis. One species will live underground, farming and building; the other will live above ground in anbundant luxury. Every hundred years or so they swap places, so don't expect to see the other species any time soon.
Mocholo is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Pinthot & Coldellini
enemies.description:
When you're an alien shapeshifter abandoned on a lifeless planet, you have to start getting creative or risk losing your marbles. These skilled shapeshifters have managed to imitate the more uncommon states of physical matter, but they can't help being beans too, it's simply too fun.
Pinthot & Coldellini is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Shapeunshifter
enemies.description:
The most successful of shapeshifters eventually become arrogant and egotistical, neglecting useful disguises in favour of more obvious tentacle-ridden forms. This is part of the natural life cycle of the species, for once they reach this point they don't tend to last much longer.
Shapeunshifter is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Space Apparition
enemies.description:
The creeping phantom of your mistakes. What if you had connected those wires faster? What if you've trusted that friend a little less? What if you put the damn card in the reader the right way the first time? Well, it's dead and you're not, so I wouldn't worry about it too much.
Space Apparition is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Sponkey
enemies.description:
These lanky aliens fancy themselves as the only truly objective species in existence, able to look at the universe without bias corrupting their perception. They are of course wrong about almost everything, but it's best not to argue - especially about pizza toppings.
Sponkey is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Spotter
enemies.description:
One of the most intelligent and technologically advanced species in the universe. However, due to their intense intellect, they have wisely decided that living in holes next to river, spearfishing, and writing poetry are the best uses of their time.
Spotter is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Steroid
enemies.description:
Sauntering statuesquely around space, these iconic robotic supermodels have inspired designs across the galaxy. Despite their glamorous looks, they have terrible table manners and respond to most questions with a blast of their ocular laser.
Steroid is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Suspicio
enemies.description:
All I see is a trash bin, a child's plastic construction toy, and a chicken nugget. These must have been added by mistake, nothing suspicious here.
Suspicio is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Suspicious Eyes
enemies.description:
They say the eyes are the windows to the soul. I'm not sure this thing has a soul, but it definitely has an unnervingly "cute" face, and a lot of gross tentacles. I'd recommend cutting them off as soon as possible and sending this murderous meat-blob to the space butchers, along with a side of Meat Beans. Also known as Granbeanlloon.
Suspicious Eyes is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica.

enemies.name: Trip Trop
enemies.description:
Some say three legs are better than two, but these spindly-limbed war machines tend to fall over frequently when attempting to conquer planets. Despite their ungainly lumbering, they've managed to "invade" seventy-five settled planets by setting up chains of low-cost supermarkets in the name of their lazy Brainoid masters.
Trip Trop is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica. It first appears as a normal boss before appearing as an enemy.

enemies.name: Victor Frankenstein
enemies.description:
This thing is the result of the descendants of the legendary Frankenstein realising that the key to reanimation lies not in the animal world, but the plant world. Using their tech they managed to revive their long-dead ancestor in a more arboreal form. Unfortunately, the seeds have spread as far as space, and for some reason they've all given themselves the same name.
Victor Frankenstein is an enemy that appears in Polus Replica. It appears both as a boss and a normal enemy.

enemies.name: Ashtart
enemies.description:
Ashtart was already deep in her grey years when she became one of the followers of Baal'Thasar. In fact, she was among the first.
She lived in fear that, on the day she died, she would have to face the judgement of some merciless god for the unspeakable sins she had committed in life.
Her desperation to avoid the inevitable led her to become the first to experiment with human sacrifices, twisted rituals, and all sorts of abhorrent practices, all at the expense of the lesser disciples of the Order of the Red Moon. She would consume their organs, wear their skin, graft their organs into herself. With every abominable act, she lost another piece of herself, and plunged her soul deeper into the depths of damnation.
As her grotesque figure wandered apathically through the halls of Red Moon Manor, her dead cold eyes forever searching for the next victim of some vile experiment, a group of terrified disciples of the Order decided to put her at the center of one instead.
It did not move. It did not even scream. The soulless abomination that Ashtart had become simply kept throwing its dagger-like stare around, searching for the next piece of flesh to consume, while its body burned in bright flames and sharp swords plunged again and again into its abhorrent mass of organs.
The relief of the disciples did not last long. The charred bones of Ashtart rose from a pile of cinders, and, somehow, even without her eyes, the disciples could feel her feral gaze picking them, one by one.
No matter how deeply her remains are buried, how thoroughly her bones are shattered, or how many exorcisms are cast upon her, Ashtart's corrupted will always comes back, clutching at anything it can control.
An unstoppable presence. Dark and hollow. Mindless and soulless. An evil presence with the singular goal of preying on life.
Ashtart is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor. She appears when the players enters the manor, and her location will be shown as a question mark (?) on the map, which will be removed after her appearance.

enemies.name: Baal'Thasar
enemies.description:
A rare philosopher with a gentle belief in the goodness of life, Baal'Thasar was also a healer and preacher who wanted to help and uplift the people around him.
And then came the first Blood Moon.
When asked what he saw during the event, Baal'Thasar's words would turn to riddles and fanatical ramblings, strange for someone once so eloquent. People said the event had driven him mad, as he began to subtly steer his teachings toward talks of eternal life and infinite irches, culminating in the founding of the Order of the Red Moon.
The truth is that the first Blood Moon blessed Baal'Thasar with a perilous gift. New eyes. Eyes that allowed him to see the duplicity, the avarice, and the selfish hunger of the people who came to him for comfort and cure. Eyes that allowed him to see life from the shallow, self-centered point of view of the desperate souls around him.
As he found himself surrounded by those dark, coiling threads of cupidity, Baal'Thasar ultimately lost sight of his own guiding light. He grased the venomous tethers with both hands, let them bind him, let all of his being become a channel for the insatiable want that he saw in the world.
Maybe he started with good intentions. Maybe he thought he could unravel the serpentine threads, eradicate them, shine his own light upon them.
But his light was quickly eclipsed, and the only thing Baal'Thasar discovered was that there is no origin and no terminus to greed. It is an insatiable, seductive beast that eats everything and serves only itself.
Baal'Thasar is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.
It is located in the west of the manor, where Congregation spawns, on the center of the labyrinth, up from the Velvet Dodecahedron. The player will find a pentagram that will teleport them to a room similar to the stage Room 1665. Where the player will fight trough hordes of enemies before fighting Baal'Thasar himself.

enemies.name: Batti Lei
enemies.description:
A winged lion with the everything of a snake. They don't hate humans, but they hate not torturing humans in a hateful manner. So turns the slightly convoluted cycle of hate.
Batti Lei is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Cane
enemies.description:
When you combine the malevolence of a corrupted ancient spirit with the honest loyalty of a humble dog, you get a creature with severe internal conflict. Evil conjurers have long wanted to fix the problem by using a corrupted dog, but there are only ever good ones.
Cane is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Congregation
enemies.description:
A shapeless mass of Red Moon disciples, Congregation was born from a ritual gone wrong.
Thirteen bodies were welded together, but only seven of the original souls remained conscious, tormented by peretual, excruciating pain. The remaining six allegedly got lucky: they died during the ritual.
The truth, unfortunately, is that the dead ones occasionally come back to life, just long enough to relive the horror of their physical form and feel its deadly, relentless pain. They bring with them terrifying memories from the hells their souls have passed through.
Before dying again, they share those hellish visions with the rest, leaving the living souls in anguish and desperation, knowing that not even death will end their suffering.
Congregation is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor. Congregation appears on the west side of the manor.
It appears on the west side of the manor, the area is a room with a square swirl pattern that gets progressively smaller and is to the north-west of the Velvet Dodecahedron. Once getting close enough, it will automatically appear.

enemies.name: Fritti
enemies.description:
The monster with the gnarliest radical color scheme! It looks like it should transform or something, or maybe you could open it up to find it's secretly an adventure playset. In reality, it enjoys slow roasting charity workers at the perfect temperature to maximally prolong their suffering. Also it sees the world in monochrome.
Fritti is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Frittoni
enemies.description:
The good news is the Frittoni doesn't cook you slow like its smaller cousin so you'll be flash fried in one painless second. The bad news is it extracts your soul first, and that thing burns for at least a couple eternities. Did you know the average human soul has five times the nerve endings of the human body? Yeah, don't piss a Frittoni off.
Frittoni is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Gianni Di Giovanni
enemies.description:
He is Gianni, fourth of his name, son of Giovanni, fifteenth of his name, grandson of Gianni, third of his name, and father of Giovanni, sixteenth of his name. The Giovanni family places lineage above all, and Gianni Giovanni the Fourth plans to be the first 322nd-generation Giovanni to marry into the Bloodmoon Clan. The fact they all quite publicly despise him hasn't put him off.
Gianni Di Giovanni is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Giovanni Di Gianni
enemies.description:
He is Giovanni, sixteenth of his name, son of Gianni, fourth of his name, grandson of Giovanni, fifteenth of his name, and father of Lil' Rhubarb. The Giovanni family places lineage above all, and Giovanni Giovanni the Sixteenth is just kind of over it. He plans to move to the beach, where he'll play keyboards in a local band who're cool with not making it big so long as they can keep just makin' music.
Giovanni Di Gianni is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: In'kuyata
enemies.description:
Among beasts borne of the Blood Moon, the In'kuyata is most majestic, crowned by its contemporaries as the New King of the Skies. The previous King of the Skies, Keith, promptly abdicated in the braying face of a gigantic winged bull and was royally gored to kibble by his successor. The Dairy Plant's reptilian rulers have placed an excessibely high bounty on the creature, presuming it may lay eggs made of milk. Or milk made of eggs. Either way, they want them juicy sky drippin's!
In'kuyata is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Jaman Jato
enemies.description:
A being made of particularly dusty dust, it is the ancient enemy of the twin deities Shaik and Vack. So goes one myth. Another says they come from the future, their dust being the ashes of those whose death they've come to show. Actually, that's a really good idea, I should be saving it for a sci-fi novella.
Dustlords of Tomorrow: Book One of the Dusts of Future Dust Trilogy, available wherever books aren't yet being burned for fuel.
Jaman Jato is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Jettatrici
enemies.description:
Deceitful sisters of misfortune who appear in places where magic gathers. It is written on tablets of expensive card stock that one sister rules the East and the other the West, feared by all in between as the Witches of the Coast.
Jettatrici is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Nagaphonata
enemies.description:
An arrogant beast, the Nagaphonata considers itself the height of taste, dismissing all others as gauche or tacky. This, coming from a snake that decorates its lair with an all-chintz aesthetic!
Nagaphonata is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Nasnasty
enemies.description:
Not even bestiary writers are spared from the cruelty of Clan Bloodmoon. They know we're all going to say this thing paid an arm and a leg for immortality, and they know full well we'll hate ourselves for it. These hack writers' nightmare are personally created by Calogero Bloodmoon, and by that I mean he pulls the limbs off zombies for fun.
Nasnasty is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Rocco
enemies.description:
It's hard to know where to start with some monsters. Are we going to point out the snake for a tail first, or save it until we get past the aerodynamically impossible elephant in the room? Actually, an elephant is better designed for flight than a bird made out of rocks, yet here we are with an avian mineral that eats children because every possible god hates us.
Rocco is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Sargon
enemies.description:
A scholar king of a long-lost empire, Sargon's ambition could never be satiated.
He could look out from the highest tower of his palace and know that every land his gaze touched belonged to him, yet still it was not enough. During the first Blood Moon, a new and twisted idea crept into his mind: if he could see the stars, then he should also own them.
His obsession with conquering the impossible dragged him further and further away from his duties as king, and so his people began to mock him as the "king of the universe".
He turned to the teachings of Baal'Thasar of the Red Moon, for eternal life was surely his right. At night, he would stare into the darkest spots in the sky. He claimed the universe whispered to him in those moments, revealing secrets and knowledge no human could ever attain alone.
With every secret learned, Sargon lost another piece of his humanity. At last, he found himself trapped in a hellish dimension: an infinite universe of his own. A universe devoid of any other life. A universe so miserable that all of its stars blaze at their brightest, consuming themselves in haste, unable to bear the anguish of bringing light to a forever lifeless void.
Now Sargon desperately tries to escape his prison. He blinks back into our world without control, only for the fabric of his universe to pull him away again. Cold stars shimmer through his fleeting form: a warning to look away.
Stare too long into Sargon's void, and you too might find yourself seduced and trapped in an infinite universe of your own.
Sargon is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor. He locates on the north on the Manor, appears after stepping on the button, and is always marked with a question mark (?) on the map.

enemies.name: Shyamalanno
enemies.description:
Originally thought to be a woman with a snake for legs, the Shyamalanno is in fact a snake with a lady for a front. but not for a head. That's what the front of a snake usualy is, isn't it? Just, like, its head? I've never thought about the front of a snake before today, and now I hate cognitive function.
Shyamalanno is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Spirit of Life
enemies.description:
The lesser frozen lake snail is capable of astral projection, albeit to such a limited degree that naked human senses can't perceive it. When enough snails gather in one place, however, they form a hive consciousness capable of manifesting fully corporeal icy shades. That's entirely made up. Still more believable than ghosts.
Spirit of Life is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Uniconiglio
enemies.description:
These long-lived cuties used to be so rare that only one captive example was recorded in a thousand years. The ancient world beheled it with awe and greeted it with "aww!" Fearing its extinction, our ancestors yearned to hear the creature's incredible mating call, produced by contracting a methane sac within its majestic horn. That was then. This is now, a few years after the second Uniconiglio was caught. Now they outnumber us five to one. Now their methane wilts our crops. Now their horny song plays eternal and it sounds like cats on fire. Now extinction seems like a good idea and we no longer care if it's us or them.
Uniconiglio is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Werehyena
enemies.description:
The damned result of a Werewolf mating with a Hyenaguy. Much like the extinct "true" hyena, Werehyenas communicate via high-pitched vocal sounds resemblind laughter. Tragically, they're almost always "laughing" in abject pain due to the effects of selective werebreeding on their bone structure.
Werehyena is an enemy that appears in Red Moon Manor.

enemies.name: Big Oni
enemies.description:
Despite the assumptions people make from their scarlet hide, red oni are amongst the most laid back and sociable of their kind. While they may sometimes devour children, they're usually decent enough to pay the parents an appropriate price.
Big Oni is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell. They are located in the caves of the mountain north of the starting area.
Big Oni takes no knockback.

enemies.name: Goshadokuro
enemies.description:
It’s a big skeleton. You want a big skeleton? Look no further buddy, this here is a big skeleton. You think you’ve seen big skeletons already? Friend, you’ve seen nothing. Don’t get no bigger than this skeleton here. Show us someone with a bigger skeleton, and we’ll show you a liar.
Goshadokuro is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.

enemies.name: Hitotsume-kozo
enemies.description:
A yokai which solicits the residents of small villages either with cursed lanterns or trays of lucky tofu. Despite its usually playful demeanour, it despises games of catch - no depth perception.
Hitotsume-kozo is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell. They are located around the village south of the starting area.

enemies.name: Kappa
enemies.description:
The slimy bottom-feeders of the yokai world, even other magical creatures are put off by their mossy breath, clammy skin and lewd predilections. Though Kappas could once be disarmed by forcing them to bow and spill their head water, the modern variety is far to uncouth to return such courtesies.
Kappa is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell. They are located at the frozen lake in the northwest of the map near the Attractorb and the river running along the south of the map near the Gold Ring.
Killing 6,000 Kappas is the requirement for unlocking Gav'Et-Oni ★.

enemies.name: Mikoshi-nyudo
enemies.description:
Fiendish trickers with a taste for human flesh, these duplicitous creatures pose as monks in order to deceive pilgrims on their paths to the holy temple. You'd think that the four foot long necks would be a giveaway, but you'd be surprised what you get away with, with a little bit of confidence.
Mikoshi-nyudo is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Mikoshi-nyudo takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Ninety-Nine Nights
enemies.description: Ninety-Nine Nights is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.

enemies.name: Orochimario
enemies.description:
Ancient legendary dragon of immense power and wisdom. With eight heads, eight tails, and a love for eightfold strong red wine, if you’re invited for a night out by it, best decline. It’ll be a nightmare to carry home.
Orochimario is a boss that appears in Mt.Moonspell at 25:00.
Defeating Orochimario in Mt.Moonspell unlocks the stage's hyper mode.
Orochimario takes reduced knockback. It is resistant to freeze, instant kill, and debuffs.

enemies.name: Spiritello
enemies.description:
There 's simply no such thing as ghosts. This is probably just a bat covered in snow, and nothing else.
Spiritello is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.

enemies.name: Tanuki
enemies.description:
Rotund trickster, always seen carrying his tail over his shoulder. Hang on, I’m getting a note passed to me. Oh. Actually it’s not his tail. Probably best you look this up yourself.
Tanuki is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell. They are located near the shrines where the Silver Ring in the north, Metaglio Right in the east, Gold Ring in the south, and Metaglio Left in the west spawn.
Tanuki takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Tengu
enemies.description:
Mysterious warriors that descend from the mountaintops to meddle in the affairs of mortals. Friend or foe, they’re always putting their nose in where it doesn’t belong.
Tengu is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Tengu takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Thunderous Oni
enemies.description:
Cunning, violent and vindictive - these demons have been known to cross mountains, seas and grand steppes in order to enact their petty revenge. Thankfully for most of their victims their poor pathfinding skills usually mean these treks are in the wrong direction.
Thunderous Oni is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Thunderous Oni takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Tsuchigumo
enemies.description:
Said to be formed from the souls of those who died in haste, cursed by a monstrous form that has enough arms to complete tasks in record speed. It’s supposed to be a curse, anyway, most of them seem to find it rather convenient.
Tsuchigumo is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Tsuchigumo takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Tsuchinoko
enemies.description:
Oh, plump wyrm of such mysterious origin. So coveted, so pleasingly squat, a delicious secret in scaly form. If I cannot have you, then may you be dashed upon the rocks by a survivor, aloof serpent!
Tsuchinoko is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.

enemies.name: Windy Oni
enemies.description:
The closest thing oni—kind have to a sage, these portly monsters hold in their thick skulls all manner of obscure ephemera. It's worth noting, of course, that most of this lore is related to how best to kill and eat various other creatures.
Windy Oni is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Windy Oni takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Yamamba
enemies.description:
Witch, monster, champion of frustrated wives; said to descend from the mountains to curse abusive fathers, husbands and monks. Perhaps due to the higher literacy rates among such people, she has nonetheless garnered a reputation as evil creature.
Yamamba is an enemy that appears in Mt.Moonspell.
Yamamba takes reduced knockback.

enemies.name: Abbadon
enemies.description:
Summoning hordes of lucusts to attack its enemies in the clergy, Abbadon has long been reviled as a sects pest. He treats plagues as performances, directing swarmed with his and as a conductor would an orchestra. Very stylish for a guy who doesn't wear trousers.
Abbadon is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania, within the final north part of the castle, and spawns when the plate with the skull symbol is pressed.
Upon defeating Abbadon for the first time, he will drop the King's Gate relic.
Defeating Abbadon while playing as Soma Cruz unlocks Yoko Belnades.

enemies.name: Akmodan II
enemies.description: Akmodan II is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Alastor
enemies.description:
Swords once possessed by the souls of violent warriors, now the warriors' souls have taken control in an altogether more frightful manner. While their spirits inhabit the sword itself, the blade casts a malevolent shadow in the form of a once living body. But who truly possesses these possessed possessions? Dracula, probably.
Alastor is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Amalaric Sniper
enemies.description:
It's fallen and it can't get up. The celestial archers were once uncanny marksmen whose arrows always struck true. The Heavens would rebalance their aim, claiming they were too overpowered.
Amalaric Sniper is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Axe Armor
enemies.description:
Sources differ on whether it's an undead soldier or an empty suit of animated armor. So far, nobody's been brave enough to get a tin opener and find out.
Axe Armor is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Beelzebub
enemies.description:
Beelzebub is a special boss enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania. It is located in the room on the farthest northwestern corner of the castle, beyond a hallway immediately to the left of the room containing the Silver Ring. However, Beelzebub cannot be fought and the door containing it cannot be opened until all the gate keys, including the Serpent Gate and Beast Gate, are obtained.
Upon defeating Beelzebub for the first time, it will drop the Pile of Secrets. On subsequent defeats, it will drop a Treasure Chest 2 containing five weapons or passive items.

enemies.name: Behemoth
enemies.description:
Its hatred keeps it moving beyond death, letting not even decomposition put an end to the grudge. They say only two things may remove Behemoth's soul from the world - the combined strength of every angel in Heaven, or therapy.
Behemoth is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
The Behemoth will drop the Rock Riot upon defeat.

enemies.name: Bitterfly
enemies.description:
The common Bitterfly has adapted to the Castle's dark caverns and perpetual night, hunting solely by sound. Due to its ears serving as wings, a Bitterfly can only hear its own flapping and frequently starves to death. The species' naturally invisible state means explorers often trip over the bodies.
Bitterfly is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Blackmore
enemies.description:
Blackmore
Blackmore is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Bloody Painting
enemies.description:
Critics have decried Brauner's series of self-portraits as "derivative", "self indulgent", and "stinking of blood". Now they're out for revenge, using what little sorcerous power still suffuses them to fling themselves at any observer and bludgeon them to death.
Bloody Painting is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Bone Ark
enemies.description:
The head is borderline useless with no applicable skills of its own, yet it holds dominion over the laborers whose backs it coasts on. It's currently entertaining high ranking job offers from a number of game publishers.
Bone Ark is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Bone Golem
enemies.description:
A terrifying amalgamation of bones, bones, and bones. More bones than can be counted, more bones than the human mind may comprehend. Within its unholy form, you can make out the remains of a big skeleton, a little skeleton, and a dog skeleton.
Bone Golem is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Bone Pillar
enemies.description:
Animated dinosaur bones originally created to make museums more interesting to kids. They succeeded with the unfortunate side effect of making museums more lethal to kids as well.
Bone Pillar is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Brachyura
enemies.description:
Brachyura is a boss enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
The Brachyura will drop the Ice Fang upon defeat.

enemies.name: Bugbear
enemies.description:
Dracula literally has eyes everywhere. Some have protested such constant surveillance as authoritarian, but the castle's master democratically resolved any controversy via public debate followed by public executions.
Bugbear is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Cave Troll
enemies.description:
Cave Troll is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
If the player defeats 3,000 enemy Cave Trolls, they would be able to unlock the Cave Troll as a playable character.

enemies.name: Company Bat
enemies.description: Company Bat is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Corpseweed
enemies.description:
An Une drawing nutrients from a corpse will take on the appearance of the corpse itself. Should that corpse ever reanimate, it will try to feed on the plant in turn, taking on the appearance of the Corpseweed which, if reanimated, will. well, let's just say horticultural necromancers love locking Unes and dead bodies in rooms together.
Corpseweed is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Death
enemies.description:
Death
Death is a special boss enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania, and is the final boss of the Ode to Castlevania expansion.

enemies.name: Devil
enemies.description:
This beast from the deepest abyss of Hell has many names, most of them registered trademarks. Speak not its blasphemous monikers, lest ye be cursed by endless litigation.
Devil is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Disc Armor
enemies.description:
Their infamous blades can be repurposed as aggressive spinning tops, around which an entire competitive scene has grown. Dracula banned such frivolity after so many minions saw their skulls severed, which might explain where are those headless skeletons are coming from.
Disc Armor is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Doppelganger
enemies.description:
A dazzlingly beautiful creature, but only sometimes. Truly confused shapeshifters that occasionally spell their name incorrectly, Dracula's magic ensures they labour under the dreadful delusion that they are the original, and that anyone who looks like them must perish. Fortunately they are incredibly predictable and manipulable combatants vulnerable to cheesy fighting techniques.
Doppelganger is a boss enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Dullahan
enemies.description:
Yet another skeleton with a detached skull. The castle administrators really need to order more superglue.
Dullahan is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Eligor
enemies.description:
A demon designed by committee. His sophisticated armor should represent infernal innovation but instead highlights the demonic tech industry's need to over engineer things regardless of efficiency. Let's not even get started on the AI features they shoehorned into it.
Eligor is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
Upon defeating Eligor for the first time, it will drop the Beast Gate relic.

enemies.name: Fishman
enemies.description: Fishman is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Flea Armor
enemies.description:
Armed and armored, a Flea Man's sprint-heeled mobility seems unhampered by the additional weight. Are their legs so unnaturally strong as to defy physics? No, they're just really into cosplay, and are stupendously skilled at shaping foam rubber.
Flea Armor is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Flea Rider
enemies.description:
Fleatis Minimus, the lesser form of what we colloquially call the "Flea Man," lacks the prodigious intellect of its more refined cousin, Fleatis Aerodynamica. Ornithologically inclines, they barbarously strike from their empyrean vantage points. This fleasaurus is really paying off.
Flea Rider is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Fleaman
enemies.description:
Fleaman
Fleaman is a special enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania. It runs across the screen instead of attacking the character.

enemies.name: Flying Skeleton
enemies.description: Flying Skeleton is an enemy that has no spawns.

enemies.name: Flying Zombie
enemies.description:
Neither death nor bisection can stop these zombies - their levitating torsos continue their pursuit of their mortal foes even after being cut in half. Dracula rips apart of his legion of zombies whenever he's feeling moody (which is always, so there are loads of these ghouls).
Flying Zombie is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Frozen Shade
enemies.description:
A chilling chandler of cheerlessness with a cold, cold heart. Frozen Shades steal the heat from victims' bodies to try and remember what it felt like to be alive, but the air around them is too frigid to keep even a sliver of thermal nostalgia.
Frozen Shade is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Gaibon
enemies.description:
Death's demonic servant has only three desires: spicy food, a horrible end to the enemies of the grim reaper, and to hang out with Slogra.
Gaibon is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania. This enemy spawns in the western part of the castle, in the corridor to the left of the first portal. This appears when you press the plate with the skull symbol.
Once defeated, the plate reappears, and pressing it a second time will spawn Slogra. Defeating Gaibon and Slogra with Grant Danasty unlocks Sypha Belnades.

enemies.name: Galamoth
enemies.description: Galamoth is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Gergoth
enemies.description:
Gergoth
Gergoth is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
It is located downstairs in the middle building below the Library, above Capra Gate, and can be defeated using Julius Belmont to unlock Soma Cruz.

enemies.name: Giant Bat
enemies.description:
Giant Bat is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.
Upon defeating the Giant Bat for the first time, it will drop the Stallion Gate relic.

enemies.name: Giant Medusa Head
enemies.description:
A Medusa Head, but massive. One rumor suggests you can do this to any Medusa Head if you ram a bicycle pump into one of her snake's mouths and start inflating. Sounds ridiculous, but we've already accepted that all gorgons are called Medusa and their heads can float around, so who can say what's silly anymore?
Giant Medusa Head is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Gorgon
enemies.description:
Bovine brutes whose breath can turn living things to stone. The milk they provide is too calcified to drink, but it's proven popular as an alternative to cement. Cheap as the stuff is, its use in the castle has led to a number of easily breakable walls.
Gorgon is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Gurkha Knife Master
enemies.description:
A Gurkha warrior with a Gurkha knife. Is the soldier named after the blade, or is the blade named for the soldier? Since the Internet hasn't been invented in this particular reality, we may never know.
Gurkha Knife Master is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Harpy
enemies.description:
The easiest way to infuriate these feathery foes is to start singing "If You're Happy and You Know It." They don't mind the cheap wordplay, but they really hate the bit where you're supposed to clap your hands.
Harpy is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Hippogryph
enemies.description:
Animal testing is ethically and morally wrong, even if said testing results in a cool hybrid of lion, eagle, and horse. Nobody is saying those experiments were right, but if we were to play Dracula's advocate. c'mon! It's like someone made a tattoo in real life!
Hippogryph is an enemy that appears in Ode to Castlevania.

enemies.name: Imp
enemies.description:
